translations.literal: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Daosheng, Zhangsun Fei
translations.idiomatic: Volume 22 Biographies 10: Zhangsun Song, Zhangsun Daosheng, Zhangsun Fei

translations.idiomatic: Biographies 10

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩

translations.literal: Zhangsun Song
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Song

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩，代人也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Song was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Song came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父仁，昭成時為南部大人。

translations.literal: His father Ren, in Zhaocheng's time, was Southern Tribal Elder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren served as Southern Tribal Elder under Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 嵩寬雅有器度，昭成賜名焉。

translations.literal: Song was broad-minded and elegant, with capacity and measure; Zhaocheng bestowed the name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Song was magnanimous and dignified; Zhaocheng gave him the name Song.

sentences.zh: 年十四，代父統事。

translations.literal: At fourteen he succeeded his father in leading affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he took his father's place in command.

sentences.zh: 昭成末年，諸部乖亂，苻堅使劉庫仁攝國事，嵩與元他等率部眾歸之。

translations.literal: In Zhaocheng's last years the tribes fell into disorder; Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to take charge of state affairs, and Song with Yuan Ta and others led their followers to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhaocheng's reign the tribes were in turmoil; Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to govern the realm, and Song with Yuan Ta and others brought their people to join him.

sentences.zh: 劉顯之謀難也，嵩率舊人及庶師七百餘家叛顯走。

translations.literal: When Liu Xian plotted treachery, Song led his old followers and the Shushi clan—more than seven hundred households—to rebel against Xian and flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian turned traitor, Song led his veterans and the Shushi, over seven hundred households, to break with Xian and escape.

sentences.zh: 將至五原，時寔君之子渥亦聚眾自立，嵩欲歸之。

translations.literal: As he was about to reach Wuyuan, Shijun's son Wo had also gathered a following and set himself up; Song wished to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Near Wuyuan, Prince Shi's son Wo had raised troops and declared himself leader; Song meant to go to him.

sentences.zh: 見於烏渥，稱逆父之子，勸嵩歸道武。

translations.literal: Meeting Wu Wo, he called Wo a son who had turned against his father and urged Song to return to Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: He met Wu Wo, who denounced Wo as a rebel against his father and urged Song to submit to Daowu.

sentences.zh: 嵩未決，烏渥回其牛首，嵩僶俛從之，見道武於二漢亭。

translations.literal: Song had not yet decided; Wu Wo turned his ox's head back, and Song bowed low and followed, meeting Daowu at Erhan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Song hesitated; Wu Wo turned his ox homeward, and Song bowed and went along, meeting Daowu at Erhan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 道武以為南部大人，累著軍功。

translations.literal: Daowu made him Southern Tribal Elder; he repeatedly distinguished himself in military service.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu appointed him Southern Tribal Elder, and he won repeated distinction in the field.

sentences.zh: 後從征中山，除冀州刺史，賜爵钜鹿公。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan, was made Governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the attack on Zhongshan, was made Governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中、司徒、相州刺史，封南平公。

translations.literal: He served in turn as Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, and was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he was Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiang Province, and was raised to Duke of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 所在著稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he earned praise.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，山陽侯奚斤、北新侯安同、白馬侯崔宏等八人坐止車門右，聽理萬機，故世號八公。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, the Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin, the Marquis of Beixin An Tong, the Marquis of Baima Cui Hong, and five others sat to the right of the imperial carriage gate and heard state affairs—hence the age called them the Eight Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan succeeded, Xi Jin of Shanyang, An Tong of Beixin, Cui Hong of Baima, and five others sat at the right of the Stop-the-Carriage Gate and governed affairs; the age called them the Eight Dukes.

sentences.zh: 晉將劉裕之伐姚泓，明元假嵩節，督山東諸軍事，傅詣平原，緣河北岸列軍，次於畔城。

translations.literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Mingyuan lent Song his staff of authority to supervise military affairs east of the mountains; he went to Pingyuan and drew up his army along the north bank of the Yellow River, encamping at Pancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu of Jin marched against Yao Hong, Mingyuan gave Song command authority over the eastern armies; he reached Pingyuan and lined his forces along the north bank of the Yellow River, camping at Pancheng.

sentences.zh: 軍頗失利。

translations.literal: The army suffered some setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign met reverses.

sentences.zh: 詔假裕道。

translations.literal: An edict granted Liu Yu passage.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict granting Liu Yu free passage.

sentences.zh: 裕於舟中望嵩麾蓋，遺以酃酒及江南食物。

translations.literal: From his boat Liu Yu saw Song's banners and canopies and sent him wine from Ling and foods of the south.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, aboard ship, sighted Song's standards and sent Ling wine and southern delicacies.

sentences.zh: 嵩皆送京師。

translations.literal: Song sent them all to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Song forwarded everything to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔嵩厚答之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Song to respond generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Song to reply in kind.

sentences.zh: 又敕簡精兵為戰備，若裕西過者，便率精銳，南出彭、沛；

translations.literal: He also commanded that picked troops be readied for war; if Yu passed westward, Song was to lead elite forces south through Peng and Pei;
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered elite troops held in readiness: if Yu marched west, Song was to drive crack units south through Peng and Pei;

sentences.zh: 如不時過，但引軍隨之。

translations.literal: if he did not pass in good time, he was only to follow with his army.
translations.idiomatic: if Yu did not pass promptly, he was merely to trail him with his army.

sentences.zh: 彼至崤、陝間，必與姚泓相持，一死一傷，眾力疲弊。

translations.literal: When Yu reached the region between Xiao and Shan, he would surely be locked with Yao Hong; one would die and one be wounded, and their forces would be worn out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached the ground between Xiao and Shan he would surely grapple with Yao Hong; one side would perish and one be crippled, and both armies exhausted.

sentences.zh: 比及秋月，徐乃乘之，則裕首可不戰而縣。

translations.literal: By autumn one could strike at leisure, and Liu Yu's head could be hung without a battle.
translations.idiomatic: Come autumn one could strike at ease, and Liu Yu's head might be taken without fighting.

sentences.zh: 於是叔孫建等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sunsun Jian and others [were dispatched].
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Sunsun Jian and others were sent.

sentences.zh: 尋河趣洛，遂入關。

translations.literal: They followed the river toward Luo and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced along the river toward Luoyang and entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 嵩與建等自城皋南濟，晉諸屯戍皆望塵奔潰。

translations.literal: Song and Jian and the rest crossed south from Chenggao; Jin garrisons everywhere fled at the dust of their approach.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Jian crossed south from Chenggao; Jin border posts broke and ran at their dust.

sentences.zh: 裕克長安，嵩乃班師。

translations.literal: When Yu took Chang'an, Song withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu seized Chang'an, Song marched home.

sentences.zh: 明元寢疾，問後事於嵩。

translations.literal: Mingyuan, lying ill, asked Song about affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan, on his sickbed, asked Song about the succession.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「立長則順，以德則人服。

translations.literal: Song said, "To install the eldest is accord with order; to install by virtue is to win men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "To set up the eldest son is to follow order; to choose by virtue is to win obedience.

sentences.zh: 今長皇子賢而世嫡，天所命也，請立。

translations.literal: Now the eldest imperial son is worthy and the legitimate heir—the mandate of Heaven; I ask that he be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest imperial son is worthy and the rightful heir; Heaven has chosen him. I beg that he be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 」乃定策，詔太武臨朝監國，嵩為左輔。

translations.literal: " The policy was settled; an edict had Taiwu attend court and oversee the state, with Song as left assistant.
translations.idiomatic: " The decision was made; Taiwu was ordered to preside at court and oversee the realm, with Song as his left-hand counselor.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，進爵北平王、司州中正。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping and Director of the Right for Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu succeeded, Song was raised to Prince of Beiping and made Director of the Right for Si Province.

sentences.zh: 詔問公卿：「赫連、蠕蠕，征討何先？

translations.literal: An edict asked the ministers, "Helian and Rouran—which should we campaign against first?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "Helian and Rouran—which should we attack first?

sentences.zh: 」嵩與平陽王長孫翰、司空奚斤等曰：「赫連土居，未能為患。

translations.literal: " Song with the Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han and the Minister of Works Xi Jin said, "Helian holds fixed territory and cannot yet be a grave threat.
translations.idiomatic: " Song, the Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han, and Minister of Works Xi Jin said, "Helian sits on settled ground and is not yet a great danger.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕世為邊害，宜先討大檀。

translations.literal: Rouran has for generations been a border scourge; we should first strike Datan.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran has long plagued the frontier; Datan should be attacked first.

sentences.zh: 及則收其畜產，足以富國；

translations.literal: If we catch him in time we can seize his herds and flocks and enrich the state;
translations.idiomatic: If we catch him in time we can take his herds and enrich the treasury;

sentences.zh: 不及則校獵陰山，多殺禽獸，皮肉筋角以充軍實，亦愈於破一小國。

translations.literal: if not, we can hunt on Yin Mountain, kill many beasts, and fill our stores with meat, hide, sinew, and horn—still better than crushing a petty state.
translations.idiomatic: if not, we can hunt Yin Mountain, slaughter game, and stock the army with meat, hides, sinew, and horn—better still than wasting force on a small realm.

sentences.zh: 」太常崔浩曰：「大檀遷徙鳥逝，疾追則不足經久，大眾則不能及之。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said, "Datan shifts like birds in flight; swift pursuit cannot be sustained long, and a great host cannot overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Ceremonies Cui Hao said, "Datan moves like a fleeing bird; hot pursuit cannot last, and a mass army cannot catch him.

sentences.zh: 赫連屈丐土宇不過千里，其刑政殘害，人神所棄，宜先討之。

translations.literal: Helian Qubugai's domain is less than a thousand li; his punishments and government are cruel—the people and spirits have cast him off; he should be attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Qubugai holds less than a thousand li; his laws are savage and men and gods have abandoned him—strike him first.

sentences.zh: 」尚書劉潔、武京侯安原請先平馮跋。

translations.literal: " The Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and the Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked that Feng Ba be pacified first.
translations.idiomatic: " Director Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan urged pacifying Feng Ba first.

sentences.zh: 帝默然，遂西巡狩。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and then made a western tour of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing and went west on inspection.

sentences.zh: 後聞屈丐死，關中大亂，議欲征之。

translations.literal: Later, hearing Qubugai had died and Guanzhong was in great disorder, they debated marching against it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when word came that Qubugai was dead and Guanzhong in chaos, the court debated a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 嵩等曰：「彼若城守，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: Song and others said, "If they hold their cities and wait at ease for our weariness,
translations.idiomatic: Song and others said, "If they shut their walls and wait while we tire ourselves,

sentences.zh: 大檀聞之，乘虛而寇，危道也。

translations.literal: when Datan hears of it he will raid in our absence—a perilous road.
translations.idiomatic: Datan will hear and strike our emptiness—that road is perilous.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃問幽征于天師寇謙之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then questioned the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi of Youzheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then consulted the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 勸行，杜超之贊成，崔浩又言西伐利。

translations.literal: Qianzhi urged the march; Du Chao seconded it; Cui Hao again argued that a western campaign would profit.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi urged action; Du Chao agreed; Cui Hao again pressed the gains of a western war.

sentences.zh: 嵩等固諫不可，帝大怒，責嵩在官貪污，使武士頓辱。

translations.literal: Song and others firmly remonstrated that it could not be done; the emperor was furious, accused Song of corruption in office, and had warriors publicly humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Song and others protested that it must not be done; the emperor raged, charged Song with corruption, and had guards shame him before the court.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 久之，加柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was additionally made Pillar of State and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was also made Pillar of State and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 自是輿駕征伐。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign,
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever the emperor marched out,

sentences.zh: 嵩以元老，多留鎮京師，坐朝堂平斷刑獄。

translations.literal: Song as an elder statesman mostly remained to guard the capital, sitting in court to judge criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Song as a senior pillar mostly stayed to guard the capital, presiding in court to decide criminal suits.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: He died at eighty; his posthumous name was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty; his posthumous name was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後孝文追錄先朝功臣，以嵩配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: Later Xiaowen recorded the merits of earlier reigns and had Song given joint sacrifice in the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaowen honored founders of earlier reigns and granted Song joint offerings in the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 子頹，善騎射，彎弓三百斤。

translations.literal: His son Tui was skilled at mounted archery and could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tui excelled in horsemanship and archery and could bend a three-hundred-jin bow.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the rank and was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 有罪黜為戍兵。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to a border soldier.
translations.idiomatic: For a crime he was reduced to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 後復爵。

translations.literal: Later his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His title was later restored.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰安王。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was An.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was An.

sentences.zh: 子敦，字孝友，位北鎮都將。

translations.literal: His son Dun, style name Xiaoyou, was Northern Garrison Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun, styled Xiaoyou, became Northern Garrison Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐黷貨，降為公。

translations.literal: For venality he was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: For corruption he was demoted from prince to duke.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，自訟先世勳重，復其王爵。

translations.literal: In Xiaowen's time he pleaded that his forebears' merit was weighty and had his princely rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaowen he argued that his ancestors' service was great and recovered his princely title.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 諡簡王。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jian.

sentences.zh: 子道，字念僧，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Dao, style name Nianseng, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 久之，隨例降為公，位左衛將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while, following the usual rule, he was reduced to duke and made Left Guards General.
translations.idiomatic: In time, by the usual rule, he was demoted to duke and made Left Guards General.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡慎。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Shen.

sentences.zh: 子悅，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yue inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 建義初，復本王爵，尋降為公，位光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he recovered his original princely rank; soon he was again reduced to duke and made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianyi he regained his princely rank; soon he was again demoted to duke and made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 五世孫儉

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant Jian
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant Jian

sentences.zh: 嵩五世孫儉，仕周知名。

translations.literal: Song's fifth-generation descendant Jian became renowned in Zhou service.
translations.idiomatic: Song's fifth-generation descendant Jian won fame serving the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 儉，本名慶明。

translations.literal: Jian's original name was Qingming.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had originally been named Qingming.

sentences.zh: 曾祖地汾，安東將軍、臨川公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Difen was General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Difen was General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖酌，恆州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhuo was Governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhuo was Governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 父戫，員外散騎侍郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Outer Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Outer Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library and died young.

sentences.zh: 儉方正有操行，神彩嚴肅，雖在私室，終日儼然。

translations.literal: Jian was square and upright in conduct, stern in bearing; even in private quarters he remained grave all day.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was upright and principled, grave in manner; even at home he sat in formal bearing all day.

sentences.zh: 性不妄交，非其同志，雖貴遊造門，亦不與相見。

translations.literal: He would not associate lightly; unless they were kindred in spirit, even noble visitors at his gate he would not receive.
translations.idiomatic: He made no casual friendships; unless they shared his principles, even grandees at his door went unseen.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，邊方騷動，儉初假東夏州防城大都督，從爾硃天光破宿勤明達等，以功賜爵索盧侯。

translations.literal: In Taichang, when the frontier was disturbed, Jian was first made Acting Grand Commander for Defense of East Xia Province; following Erzhu Tianhe he defeated Su Qin Mingda and others and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Suolu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era, when the border stirred, Jian was first Acting Grand Commander for Defense of East Xia Province; he followed Erzhu Tianhe in defeating Su Qin Mingda and was enfeoffed Marquis of Suolu.

sentences.zh: 周文臨夏州，以為錄事參軍事，深敬器之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen came to Xia Province he made Jian Recording Secretary and greatly respected and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wen arrived at Xia Province he made Jian Recording Secretary and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳被害，周文赴平涼，凡有經綸謀策，儉皆參預。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was killed, Zhou Wen went to Pingliang; whenever there was strategy for governing the realm, Jian took part.
translations.idiomatic: After Heba Yue was slain, Zhou Wen went to Pingliang; on every plan for rule Jian was consulted.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，留儉為秦州長史、防城大都督，委以後事，別封信都縣伯。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Hou Mo Chen Yue, Jian was left as Chief Administrator of Qin Province and Grand Commander for Defense, entrusted with affairs behind the lines, and additionally enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Mo Chen Yue was pacified, Jian was left Chief Administrator of Qin and Grand Commander for Defense, entrusted with the rear, and enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 渭州刺史可硃渾元奔東魏後，河渭間人情離阻。

translations.literal: After Governor of Wei Province Kezhu Hunyuan fled to Eastern Wei, hearts between the Yellow and Wei rivers were divided.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Governor Kezhu Hunyuan fled to Eastern Wei, loyalty between the Yellow and Wei rivers frayed.

sentences.zh: 刺史李弼令儉權鎮渭州。

translations.literal: Governor Li Bi had Jian act as temporary commander of Wei Province.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Bi put Jian in temporary charge of Wei Province.

sentences.zh: 儉將十餘騎冒難赴之。

translations.literal: Jian took a dozen horsemen and braved hardship to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Jian rode out with a dozen men through danger to reach it.

sentences.zh: 復隨機安撫，羌胡悅服。

translations.literal: He then soothed according to circumstances; Qiang and Hu submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified as the moment required; Qiang and Hu submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 轉夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 甚得人和。

translations.literal: He won great harmony among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He won deep goodwill among the people.

sentences.zh: 時西夏州仍未內屬，而東魏遣許和為刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Western Xia Province had still not submitted within the realm, while Eastern Wei sent Xu He as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia Province had not yet joined the realm; Eastern Wei sent Xu He as its governor.

sentences.zh: 儉以信義招之，和乃歸附。

translations.literal: Jian won him by faith and righteousness; He then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian won him with faith and duty; He then came over.

sentences.zh: 即以儉為西夏州刺史，總統三夏州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Jian was at once made Governor of Western Xia and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the three Xia provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made Governor of Western Xia and supreme commander of the three Xia provinces.

sentences.zh: 荊襄初附，周文表授儉都督三荊等十二州諸軍事、荊州刺史、東南道行台僕射。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang first submitted, Zhou Wen memorialized to appoint Jian Commander-in-Chief of twelve provinces including the three Jings, Governor of Jing, and Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang first submitted, Zhou Wen memorialized making Jian commander of twelve provinces including the three Jings, Governor of Jing, and Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit.

sentences.zh: 所部鄭縣令泉璨為百姓所訟，推按獲實。

translations.literal: Magistrate Quan Can of Zheng County in his jurisdiction was sued by the people; investigation proved the charges true.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Zheng County, Quan Can, was accused by the people and investigation proved him guilty.

sentences.zh: 儉即大集寮屬，遂於査事前引己過，肉袒自罰，舍璨不問。

translations.literal: Jian at once gathered his staff, then before the investigation hall cited his own fault, bared his torso and punished himself, and let Can go without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Jian immediately assembled his staff, confessed his own fault before the investigation hall, stripped and flogged himself, and released Can without punishment.

sentences.zh: 於是屬城肅勵，莫敢犯法。

translations.literal: Thereafter subordinate cities were stirred to discipline and none dared break the law.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate districts were awed into order and none dared offend the law.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝璽書勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei sent an imperial letter commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei sent a sealed letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 周文又與儉書曰：「近聞公部內縣令有罪，遂自杖三十，用肅群下，聞之嘉歎良久不可言。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen also wrote to Jian, saying, "Recently I heard that a magistrate in your jurisdiction had committed an offense, and you yourself administered thirty strokes to discipline your subordinates; on hearing it I rejoiced and sighed for a long time, beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen also wrote to Jian: "I have just heard that a magistrate under you offended, and you yourself took thirty strokes to awe your staff. I rejoiced and sighed a long while at the news—words fail me.

sentences.zh: 」儉清正率下，兼懷仁恕。

translations.literal: " Jian was upright in leading subordinates and combined sternness with humane tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian led with integrity and mixed strictness with mercy.

sentences.zh: 有竊盜者，原情得實，誨而放之。

translations.literal: When thieves were caught, if the facts allowed mercy he admonished and released them.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves were taken, if circumstances warranted leniency he lectured them and let them go.

sentences.zh: 荊蠻舊俗，少不敬長。

translations.literal: The old custom of Jing barbarians was scant respect for elders.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Jing tribes the old custom slighted elders.

sentences.zh: 儉殷勤勸導，風俗大革。

translations.literal: Jian urged them earnestly; the custom was greatly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian urged them patiently; the custom changed deeply.

sentences.zh: 務廣耕桑，兼習武事，故邊境無虞，人安其業。

translations.literal: He pressed broad planting and sericulture and also trained in military affairs, so the border was untroubled and the people secure in their trades.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted farming and silkworms and trained the people in arms, so the frontier knew no alarm and men kept their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 吏人表請為儉構清德樓，樹碑刻頌，朝議許之。

translations.literal: Officials and people petitioned to build a Tower of Pure Virtue for Jian and set up a stele with laudatory inscription; court deliberation approved.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners asked to raise a Tower of Pure Virtue for Jian and carve a praise stele; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 吏人又以儉秩滿，恐有代至，詣闕乞留儉，朝廷嘉而許之，在州遂曆七載。

translations.literal: Officials and people also feared a successor when Jian's term ended and went to the capital to beg that Jian remain; the court praised this and agreed, and he governed the province for seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: When his term neared its end the people feared a replacement and petitioned at court to keep Jian; the throne approved, and he held the province seven years running.

sentences.zh: 徵授大行台尚書，兼相府司馬。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently Chief Secretary of the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Director of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently Chief Secretary to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 常與群公侍坐，及退，周文謂左右曰：「此人閒雅，孤每與語，常肅然畏敬，恐有所失。

translations.literal: He often sat with the nobles in attendance; when they withdrew, Zhou Wen told his attendants, "This man is refined; whenever I speak with him I always stand in solemn awe, fearing I may fail him.
translations.idiomatic: He often sat with the great lords in audience; when they left, Zhou Wen told his attendants, "This man is grave and elegant; every talk with him leaves me in respectful fear lest I fall short.

sentences.zh: 」他日，周文謂儉曰：「名實須相稱，尚書志安貧素，可改名儉，以彰雅操。

translations.literal: " Another day Zhou Wen told Jian, "Name and reality must match; as Director you aspire to poverty and plainness—you may change your name to Jian to display your refined conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " Another day Zhou Wen said to Jian, "Name and deed must accord. As Director you love poverty and simplicity; take the name Jian to show your character.

sentences.zh: 」遷尚書左僕射，加侍中。

translations.literal: " He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後除東南道行台僕射、大都督十五州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander of fifteen provinces' military affairs, and Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander of fifteen provinces, and Governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 時梁岳陽王蕭詧內附，初遣使入朝。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Yueyang of Liang, Xiao Cha, submitted within the realm and first sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, came over, he first sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 至荊州，儉於査事列軍儀，具戎服，以賓主禮見使。

translations.literal: When they reached Jing Province, Jian arrayed military ceremony at the investigation hall, put on full armor, and received the envoys with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou, Jian drew up military formation at the investigation hall, wore full armor, and received the envoys as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，音聲如鐘，大為鮮卑語，遣人傳譯以答問。

translations.literal: Of imposing stature, his voice like a bell, he spoke much in Xianbei and had men interpret to answer their questions.
translations.idiomatic: Towering in build, voice like a bell, he spoke largely in Xianbei and had interpreters relay his replies.

sentences.zh: 客惶恐不敢仰視。

translations.literal: The envoys were fearful and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys trembled and dared not raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 日晚，儉乃著裙襦紗帽，引客宴於別齋。

translations.literal: At evening Jian put on skirt, jacket, and gauze cap and entertained the guests in a side hall.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he changed to skirt, jacket, and gauze cap and feasted them in a side chamber.

sentences.zh: 因敘梁國喪亂，朝廷招攜之意，發言可觀。

translations.literal: He then spoke of Liang's turmoil and the court's wish to win men over; his words were striking.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of Liang's chaos and the court's wish to gather the loyal; his words impressed.

sentences.zh: 使人大悅，出曰：「吾所不能測也。」

translations.literal: The envoys were greatly pleased and on leaving said, "What we could not measure in him."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were delighted and said on leaving, "We could not fathom such a man."

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，授東南道大都督、荊襄等三十三州鎮防諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was made Grand Commander of the Southeast Circuit and military commander for the defense of thirty-three provinces including Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was Grand Commander of the Southeast and defender of thirty-three provinces including Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 及梁元帝嗣位於江陵，外敦鄰睦，內懷異計。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang succeeded at Jiangling, outwardly he was cordial with neighbors but inwardly he harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiangling he was courteous abroad but schemed within.

sentences.zh: 儉密啟陳攻取之謀。

translations.literal: Jian secretly memorialized a plan to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian secretly proposed a plan to take him.

sentences.zh: 於是徵儉入朝，問以經略。

translations.literal: Jian was then summoned to court and questioned on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and asked for strategy.

sentences.zh: 儉陳謀，周文深然之，乃命還州，密為之備。

translations.literal: Jian laid out his plan; Zhou Wen deeply approved and ordered him back to his province to prepare in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Jian presented his design; Zhou Wen strongly agreed and sent him back to prepare in secret.

sentences.zh: 尋令柱國於謹伐江陵。

translations.literal: Soon the pillar of state Yu Jin was ordered to attack Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Pillar of State Yu Jin was sent against Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 事平，以儉元謀，賞奴婢三百口。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, for Jian's original plan he was rewarded with three hundred households of slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: After victory, for Jian's original plan he received three hundred households of slaves and maids.

sentences.zh: 遂令儉鎮江陵，進爵昌寧郡公。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to garrison Jiangling and advanced to Duke of Changning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to hold Jiangling and was raised to Duke of Changning.

sentences.zh: 後移鎮荊州，授總管荊襄等五十二州諸軍事、行荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was shifted to garrison Jing Province and made overall commander of fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang and Acting Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he shifted to Jing Province as overall commander of fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang and Acting Governor.

sentences.zh: 及周閔帝初，趙貴等將圖晉公護，儉長子僧衍預其謀，坐死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Min of Zhou, Zhao Gui and others plotted against the Duke of Jin, Hu; Jian's eldest son Sengyan took part in the plot and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Min of Zhou, Zhao Gui and others plotted against the Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu; Jian's eldest son Sengyan joined them and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 護乃徵儉，拜小塚宰。

translations.literal: Hu then summoned Jian and made him Junior Director of the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Hu then summoned Jian and made him Junior Director of the Imperial Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，拜柱國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was made Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was made Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 朝議以儉操行清白，勳績隆重，乃下詔褒美之，兼賜以雜采粟麥，以彰其美。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that Jian's conduct was pure and his merit weighty; an edict praised him and additionally bestowed mixed silks and grain to display his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Jian's conduct pure and his service great; an edict praised him and gave silks and grain to honor his virtue.

sentences.zh: 天和初，轉陝州，總管七州諸軍事、陝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was transferred to Shan Province, overall commander of seven provinces and Governor of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was transferred to Shan Province as commander of seven provinces and its governor.

sentences.zh: 儉嘗詣闕奏事，時大雪，雪中待報，自旦達暮，竟無惰容。

translations.literal: Jian once came to court to report; it was snowing heavily, and he waited in the snow for a reply from dawn to dusk without a sign of slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Once, coming to report at court in heavy snow, he waited for answer from dawn to dusk without slackening.

sentences.zh: 其謹愨若此。

translations.literal: Such was his scrupulous caution.
translations.idiomatic: So scrupulous was he.

sentences.zh: 以疾還京，詔以儉舊居狹隘，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: Ill, he returned to the capital; an edict said Jian's old dwelling was cramped and granted him a first-rank mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When illness sent him to the capital, an edict found his old house too small and gave him a mansion of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 後薨于夏州總管。

translations.literal: Later he died while overall commander at Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as overall commander at Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺令：斂以時服，素車載柩，不設儀仗，親友贈襚，一無所受。

translations.literal: His final instructions: burial in timely dress, plain cart for the coffin, no ceremonial guard, and no gifts of burial goods from kin and friends were to be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His last charge: bury him in ordinary dress, carry the coffin in a plain cart without guard of honor, and accept no funeral gifts from kin or friends.

sentences.zh: 諸子並奉行之。

translations.literal: His sons all followed this.
translations.idiomatic: His sons obeyed in full.

sentences.zh: 又遺啟請葬周文帝陵側，並以所賜宅還官，詔皆從之。

translations.literal: He also left a memorial asking burial beside Zhou Wen's tomb and that the granted house be returned to the state; the edicts all granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to be buried beside Zhou Wen and to return the granted house to the state; both were approved.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加涼瓜等十州諸軍事、涼州刺史，追封鄫國公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former offices, additionally made commander of ten provinces including Liang and Gua and Governor of Liang, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zeng, posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his former offices posthumously, was made commander of ten provinces including Liang and Gua and Governor of Liang, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zeng with posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 荊州人儀同趙超等六百九十七人，詣闕請為儉立廟樹碑，詔許之。

translations.literal: Six hundred ninety-seven men of Jing Province, including Yitong Zhao Chao, went to court to ask a temple and stele for Jian; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred ninety-seven men of Jing Province, including Zhao Chao, petitioned for a temple and stele; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，詔曰：「故柱國、鄫國公儉，臨終審正，爰吐德音。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande an edict said, "The late Pillar of State, Duke of Zeng Jian, at death was careful and upright and uttered words of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande an edict said, "The late Pillar of State, Duke of Zeng Jian, facing death was exact in virtue and spoke words of integrity.

sentences.zh: 以所居之宅本因上賜，制度宏麗，非諸子所居，請以還官，更遷他所。

translations.literal: The house he dwelt in was originally bestowed by the throne, grand in scale and not fit for his sons to inhabit; he asked that it be returned to the state and that they move elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The house he lived in had been a royal gift, splendid beyond what his sons should keep; he asked to return it and move elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 昔叔敖辭沃壤之地，蕭何就窮僻之鄉。

translations.literal: In antiquity Sunshu Ao refused rich soil and Xiao He took a poor hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Sunshu Ao of old refused fertile land; Xiao He chose a mean district.

sentences.zh: 以古方令，無慚曩哲。

translations.literal: Measured against antiquity and the present, he need not blush before the sages of old.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient and modern measure he need not blush before the wise of old.

sentences.zh: 而有司未達大體，遽以其第外給。

translations.literal: Yet the offices did not grasp the larger meaning and hastily gave the mansion to outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offices missed the larger point and quickly gave the mansion away.

sentences.zh: 夫追善念功，先王令典，豈得遂其謙挹，致乖懲勸！

translations.literal: To recall merit and cherish the good is the ancient kings' constant rule—how could one indulge his humility and fail in reward and encouragement!
translations.idiomatic: To honor merit is the ancient kings' law—how indulge his modesty and break the rule of reward!

sentences.zh: 令以本宅還其妻子，俾清風遠播，無替聿修。」

translations.literal: Let the original house be returned to his wife and sons, so that pure wind may spread far and his fine conduct never fade."
translations.idiomatic: Let the house return to his wife and sons, so his purity may spread far and his virtue never fade."

sentences.zh: 次子隆，位司金中大夫。

translations.literal: Second son Long held office as Director within the Ministry of Metals.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Long was Director within the Ministry of Metals.

sentences.zh: 從長潮西元定代陳，沒江南，卒。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Chang on the western campaign against Chen, he was captured south of the Yangtze and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Chang west against Chen, was lost south of the Yangtze, and died there.

sentences.zh: 隆弟平，最知名。

translations.literal: Long's younger brother Ping was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Long's younger brother Ping was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 儉子平

translations.literal: Jian's son Ping
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Ping

sentences.zh: 平字處均，美容儀，有器幹，頗覽書記，為周衛王侍讀。

translations.literal: Ping, style name Chujun, was handsome in bearing, had capacity and ability, read widely in documents, and was Reader to the Prince of Wei of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, styled Chujun, was handsome and capable, well read in records, and Reader to Zhou's Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 時武帝逼于宇文護，與衛王謀誅之，王常使平通意於帝。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor Wu was pressed by Yuwen Hu; with the Prince of Wei he plotted to kill Hu, and the prince often had Ping convey his intent to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu was constrained by Yuwen Hu; he and the Prince of Wei plotted Hu's death, and the prince often sent Ping to speak for him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 護誅，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Ping was made Opening Office, Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was killed, Ping was made Opening Office, Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.

sentences.zh: 宣帝置東京官屬，以平為少司寇，與宗伯趙芬分掌六府。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan set up Eastern Capital offices and made Ping Junior Minister of Justice, sharing the six ministries with the Minister of Rites Zhao Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan established Eastern Capital offices and made Ping Junior Minister of Justice, sharing the six ministries with Zhao Fen, Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 隋文龍潛時，與平情好款洽。

translations.literal: When Wen of Sui was still rising, he and Ping were on intimate terms.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was still in the wings, he and Ping were close friends.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，恩禮彌厚。

translations.literal: When Wen became Chancellor, his favor and courtesy grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen became Chancellor, favor and courtesy deepened.

sentences.zh: 時賀若弼鎮壽陽，帝恐其懷貳，遣平代之為揚州總管，賜爵襄陽公。

translations.literal: At that time He Ruo Bi guarded Shouyang; the emperor feared disloyalty and sent Ping to replace him as Overall Commander of Yang Province and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi then held Shouyang; Wen feared treason and sent Ping to replace him as Overall Commander of Yang Province and made him Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 弼果不從，平麾壯士執弼，送京師。

translations.literal: Bi indeed would not obey; Ping commanded stalwarts to seize Bi and send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bi refused obedience; Ping sent strong men to seize him and escort him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇三年，徵拜度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang of Sui he was summoned as Director of the Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's third year of Kaihuang he was summoned as Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 平見天下州縣多罹水旱，百姓不給，奏令人間每秋家出粟麥一石以下，貧富為差，儲之閭里，以備凶年，名曰義倉。

translations.literal: Ping saw that prefectures and counties everywhere suffered flood and drought and the people lacked sustenance; he memorialized that each autumn every household should contribute grain and wheat below one picul, rich and poor by gradation, stored in the hamlet against famine—called righteous granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing floods and droughts everywhere and the people in want, he memorialized that each autumn every household should set aside up to one picul of grain and wheat by wealth, stored in the village against famine—righteous granaries.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 自是州裏豐衍。

translations.literal: From then on the districts were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Districts thereafter grew plentiful.

sentences.zh: 後轉工部尚書，名曰稱職。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Director of Works and was called competent in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Director of Works and was judged fit for office.

sentences.zh: 時有人告大都督邴紹非毀朝庭為憒憒者，上怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: Then someone reported that Grand Commander Bing Shao had slandered the court as muddled; the emperor was angry and would execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported Grand Commander Bing Shao had mocked the court as muddled; the emperor raged and would kill him.

sentences.zh: 平進諫曰：「諺云：'不癡不聾，不作大家翁。

translations.literal: Ping remonstrated, saying, "The proverb says, 'Without deafness or foolishness one cannot be the head of a great house.'
translations.idiomatic: Ping remonstrated: "The proverb says, 'Without deafness or folly one cannot head a great household.'

sentences.zh: '此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: ' Though the words are small, they can illustrate what is large.
translations.idiomatic: ' This saying is small, yet it applies to great matters.

sentences.zh: 邴紹之言，不應聞奏。

translations.literal: Bing Shao's words should not have been reported to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's words should never have reached Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下又復誅之，恐百代之後，有虧聖德。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty also executes him, I fear a hundred generations hence your sacred virtue will suffer."
translations.idiomatic: If you kill him too, I fear posterity will find a stain on your sacred virtue.

sentences.zh: 」上於是赦紹。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon pardoned Shao.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pardoned Shao.

sentences.zh: 因敕群臣，誹謗之罪，勿復以聞。

translations.literal: He then commanded the ministers that crimes of slander need not be reported.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered that slander need not be reported.

sentences.zh: 後突厥達頭可汗與都藍可汗相攻，各遣使請援。

translations.literal: Later the Tujue khagans Datou and Dulan fought each other; each sent envoys asking aid.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Tujue khagans Datou and Dulan fought; each asked for aid.

sentences.zh: 上遣平持節宣諭，令其和解。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Ping with staff of authority to proclaim and urge reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ping with authority to proclaim peace.

sentences.zh: 平至，陳利害，遂各解兵。

translations.literal: When Ping arrived he set forth gain and harm; they thereupon each disbanded their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ping explained profit and peril; both then stood down.

sentences.zh: 可汗贈平馬二百疋。

translations.literal: The khagans gave Ping two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The khagans gave him two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 還，進所得馬，上盡以賜之。

translations.literal: On his return he presented the horses received; the emperor gave them all back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he offered the horses; the emperor returned them all to Ping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遇譴，以尚書檢校汴州事，尋除汴州刺史，後曆許、貝二州，俱有善政。

translations.literal: Before long he met with censure, was made Director on inspection of Bian Province affairs, soon made Governor of Bian, and later served Xu and Bei in turn—everywhere with good government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was censured, made Director inspecting Bian, then Governor of Bian, and later Xu and Bei—good rule in each.

sentences.zh: 鄴都俗薄，前後刺史，多不稱職。

translations.literal: The customs of Ye were shallow; former governors mostly failed in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's folk were fickle; earlier governors mostly failed.

sentences.zh: 朝庭以平為相州刺史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: The court made Ping Governor of Xiang Province; he won a strong reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Ping Governor of Xiang; he won great fame for competence.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，坐正月十五日百姓大戲，畫衣裳鍪甲象，上怒免之。

translations.literal: After several years in the province, on the fifteenth day of the first month the people staged a great play with painted robes, helmets, and armor as spectacle; the emperor in anger dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: After years in office, on the fifteenth of the first month the people staged a great show in painted armor; the emperor in anger removed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而上念平鎮淮南時事，進位大將軍，拜太常卿、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor recalled Ping's service guarding the Huai south and advanced him to Grand General, made Minister of Ceremonies and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon remembering Ping's guard of the Huai, the emperor raised him to Grand General and made him Minister of Ceremonies and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 子師孝，性輕狡好利，數犯法。

translations.literal: His son Shixiao was light and crafty, greedy for gain, and repeatedly broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiao was frivolous and greedy and broke the law again and again.

sentences.zh: 上以其不克負荷，遣使吊平。

translations.literal: The emperor, judging him unfit to bear the burden, sent envoys to mourn Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Judging him unfit to carry the house, the emperor sent envoys to mourn Ping.

sentences.zh: 以師孝為勃海郡主簿。

translations.literal: Shixiao was made Chief Clerk of Bohai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiao was made Chief Clerk of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 屬大業之季，恣行貪濁，一郡苦之。

translations.literal: In the late Daye era he indulged in greed and corruption and the whole commandery suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In late Daye he plundered freely and the commandery groaned.

sentences.zh: 後為王世充所害。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 長孫道生

translations.literal: Zhangsun Daosheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Daosheng

sentences.zh: 道生廉約，身為三司，而衣不華飾，食不兼味。

translations.literal: Daosheng was frugal and plain; though he held rank as one of the Three Excellencies, his clothes were not ornate and his food had no second flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng lived plainly; though one of the Three Excellencies, he wore no finery and ate no second dish.

sentences.zh: 一熊皮鄣泥，數十年不易，時人比之晏嬰。

translations.literal: A single bear-hide mudguard—decades without change; men of the time compared him to Yan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: One bear-hide mud-guard he kept decades unchanged; his age compared him to Yan Ying.

sentences.zh: 第宅卑陋。

translations.literal: His residence was low and mean.
translations.idiomatic: His house was humble.

sentences.zh: 出鎮後，其子弟頗更修繕，起堂廡。

translations.literal: After he went out to command on the frontier, his sons and younger kin somewhat repaired it and raised halls and corridors.
translations.idiomatic: After he marched out, his sons repaired it and raised halls and galleries.

sentences.zh: 道生還，歎曰：「昔霍去病以匈奴未滅，無有家為。

translations.literal: When Daosheng returned he sighed, "In the past Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed he would not build a home.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Daosheng sighed: "Huo Qubing once said that while the Xiongnu were unbeaten he would not make a home.

sentences.zh: 今強寇尚遊魂漠北，吾豈可安坐華美也！

translations.literal: " Now strong foes still wander the northern wastes—how can I sit at ease in splendor!
translations.idiomatic: Now fierce enemies still roam the northern desert—how can I dwell in comfort and splendor!

sentences.zh: 」乃切責子弟，令毀其宅。

translations.literal: " He sharply reproved his sons and ordered the house destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He sharply rebuked his sons and had the house torn down.

sentences.zh: 太武世，所在著績，每建大議，多合時機。

translations.literal: In Taiwu's time wherever he served he won achievement; whenever he raised great counsel it mostly fit the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiwu he distinguished himself wherever he served; his great counsels usually matched the time.

sentences.zh: 為將有權略，善待士眾。

translations.literal: As a general he had stratagem and kindly treated officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he was resourceful and kind to troops.

sentences.zh: 帝命歌工曆頌群臣曰：「智如崔浩，廉如道生。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered singing masters to praise the ministers in turn, saying, "Wise as Cui Hao, incorrupt as Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had singers praise his ministers in turn: "Wise as Cui Hao, pure as Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 」及年老，頗惑其妻孟氏，以此見譏。

translations.literal: " When old he was much swayed by his wife Lady Meng and for this was mocked.
translations.idiomatic: " In old age he was much ruled by his wife Lady Meng and was ridiculed for it.

sentences.zh: 與從父嵩俱為三公，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: He and his cousin Song both held the Three Excellencies—a glory of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He and his cousin Song both reached the Three Excellencies—the glory of their day.

sentences.zh: 子瓬，位少卿，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xian held office as Vice Minister; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian was Vice Minister and died young.

sentences.zh: 瓬子觀，少以壯勇知名，後襲祖爵上党王。

translations.literal: Xian's son Guan in youth was famed for bold courage; later he inherited his grandfather's title as Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Guan was famed in youth for courage; later he inherited the title Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時異姓諸王襲爵，多降為公，帝以其祖道生佐命先朝，故特不降。

translations.literal: At that time alien surnames inheriting titles were mostly reduced to duke; the emperor because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding court in an earlier reign specially did not reduce him.
translations.idiomatic: Alien princes were usually demoted to duke; because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding reign, the emperor did not demote him.

sentences.zh: 以征西大將軍、假司空，督河西七鎮諸軍討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: As General Who Pacifies the West and Acting Minister of Works he supervised military affairs of the seven western garrisons in a campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: As General Who Pacifies the West and Acting Minister of Works he commanded the seven western garrisons against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 部帥拾寅遁藏，焚其所居城邑而還。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Shiyin fled and hid, burning the cities he had held before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Shiyin fled and hid, burning his cities before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，拜殿中尚書、侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowen's accession he was Director of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾又侵逼，復假觀司空討降之。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun again pressed the border, he was again lent the Acting Ministry of Works to campaign and subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun invaded again he was again lent the seal of Acting Minister of Works to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 後為征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Ding.

sentences.zh: 葬禮依其祖靖王故事，陪葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: His funeral followed the precedent of his grandfather the Tranquil Prince and he was buried at the Clouds-in-the-Middle Golden Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral followed his grandfather the Tranquil Prince and he was buried at the Golden Tomb in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 曾孫幼

translations.literal: Great-grandson You
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson You

sentences.zh: 子冀歸，六歲襲爵，降為公。

translations.literal: His son Jigui at six inherited the title and was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jigui at six inherited the title and was demoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 孝文以其幼承家業，賜名幼，字承業。

translations.literal: Xiaowen because he bore the family charge while young bestowed the name You, style Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen, seeing him bear the house while still young, gave him the name You, styled Chengye.

sentences.zh: 承業聰敏有才藝，虛心愛士，為前將軍，從孝文南討。

translations.literal: Chengye was clever and talented, humble and fond of scholars; as Forward General he followed Xiaowen on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye was clever, talented, humble, and loved scholars; as Forward General he followed Xiaowen south.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，為揚州刺史、假鎮南大將軍、都督淮南諸軍事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time he was Governor of Yang Province, Acting General Who Guards the South, and commander of Huainan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Yang, Acting General Who Guards the South, and commander of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 梁將裴邃、虞鴻襲據壽春，承業諸子驍果，邃頗難之，號曰：「鐵小兒」。

translations.literal: The Liang generals Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized Shouchun; Chengye's sons were fierce and Sui found them hard to face, calling them the "little irons."
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized Shouchun; Chengye's sons were ferocious and Sui called them the "little irons."

sentences.zh: 詔河間王琛總眾援之。

translations.literal: An edict had the Prince of Hejian lead the host to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Prince of Hejian to lead reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 琛欲決戰，承業以雨久，更須持重。

translations.literal: The prince wished to give battle; Chengye because rain had lasted long urged greater caution.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wanted battle; Chengye, with rains prolonged, urged patience.

sentences.zh: 琛弗從，遂戰，為賊所乘，承業後殿。

translations.literal: The prince would not listen and gave battle; the enemy seized the chance; Chengye brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused, fought, was exploited by the foe; Chengye covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 初，承業既總強兵，久不決戰，議者疑有異圖。

translations.literal: At first, because Chengye held strong troops and long refused battle, critics suspected other designs.
translations.idiomatic: At first, since Chengye held a strong host and would not fight, some suspected ulterior motives.

sentences.zh: 朝庭重遣河間王琛及臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等三都督，外聲助承業，內實防之。

translations.literal: The court again sent the Prince of Hejian, the Prince of Huaiyang Yu, and Director of the Masters of Writing Li Xian as three commanders—in name to aid Chengye, in fact to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the Prince of Hejian, Prince of Huaiyang Yu, and Li Xian as three commanders—ostensibly to help Chengye, in truth to watch him.

sentences.zh: 會鮮于修禮反於中山，以承業為大都督北討。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Zhongshan, Chengye was made Grand Commander for the Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Zhongshan, Chengye was made Grand Commander of the Northern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 尋以本使達鄴城，詔承業解行台，罷大使，遣河間王琛為大都督，酈道元為行台。

translations.literal: Soon, reaching Ye as chief envoy, an edict relieved Chengye of the mobile secretariat, removed his grand envoy status, and sent the Prince of Hejian as Grand Commander and Li Daoyuan as mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, reaching Ye as chief envoy, an edict stripped him of the mobile secretariat and grand envoy rank and made the Prince of Hejian Grand Commander with Li Daoyuan as secretariat.

sentences.zh: 承業遣子子裕奉表，稱與琛同在淮南，俱當國難。

translations.literal: Chengye sent his son Ziyu with a memorial saying he and the prince were together in Huainan and both faced the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye sent his son Ziyu with a memorial: he and the prince were both in Huainan facing national crisis.

sentences.zh: 琛敗臣全，遂生私隙。

translations.literal: The prince was defeated while he remained whole, and private rancor arose.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was beaten while he stayed intact, and private bitterness grew.

sentences.zh: 且臨機奪帥，非策所長。

translations.literal: Moreover, seizing command on the eve of battle was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, snatching command at the critical hour was no skill of his.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 琛與承業前到呼沲，承業未欲戰，而琛不從。

translations.literal: The prince and Chengye advanced to Hulu; Chengye did not wish to fight and the prince would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince and Chengye reached Hulu; Chengye would not fight and the prince would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 行達五鹿，為修禮邀擊，琛不赴之，賊總至，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Marching to Wulu they were ambushed by Xiuli; the prince would not go to their aid; the rebels gathered and they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulu, Xiuli ambushed them; the prince would not aid; rebels massed and they were routed.

sentences.zh: 承業與琛並除名。

translations.literal: Chengye and the prince were both struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye and the prince were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋而正平郡蜀反，復假承業鎮西將軍、討蜀都督。

translations.literal: Soon the commandery of Zhengping in Shu rebelled; Chengye was again lent General Who Pacifies the West and Commander for the Shu Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhengping in Shu rebelled; Chengye was again lent General Who Pacifies the West and Commander against Shu.

sentences.zh: 頻戰有功，除平東將軍，復本爵。

translations.literal: Repeated battles brought merit; he was made General Who Pacifies the East and his original title restored.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated victories won him General Who Pacifies the East and restoration of his title.

sentences.zh: 後除尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，復以承業為行台討之。

translations.literal: Before long, Governor of Yong Province Xiao Baoyin held the province in rebellion; Chengye was again made mobile secretariat to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yong Governor Xiao Baoyin rebelled; Chengye was again mobile secretariat against him.

sentences.zh: 承業時背疽未愈，靈太后勞之曰：「卿疹源如此，朕欲相停，更無可寄，如何？

translations.literal: Chengye's back abscess had not healed; Empress Dowager Ling comforted him, "Your ailment runs so deep; I wished to rest you, yet there is no other to entrust—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye's back sore was unhealed; Empress Dowager Ling said, "Your wound is so grave I wished to let you rest, yet none else can be trusted—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」承業答曰：「死而後已，敢不自力。

translations.literal: Chengye answered, "After death one stops—how dare I not exert myself?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye answered, "I serve until death—how dare I not strive?"

sentences.zh: 」時子彥亦患腳癉，扶杖入辭。

translations.literal: At that time his son Yan also had foot sores; leaning on a staff he came to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan had foot sores too; leaning on a staff he came to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射元順顧相謂曰：「吾等備為大臣，各居寵位，危難之日，病者先行，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan Shun looked at his peers and said, "We are prepared as great ministers, each in favor—on a day of peril should the sick go first? Is that not wrong!"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Shun said to his fellows, "We stand as chief ministers in favor—on a day of danger must the sick lead the way? Can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 」莫有對者。

translations.literal: None replied.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 時薛鳳賢反于正平，薛修義屯聚河東，分據鹽池，攻圍蒲阪，東西連結，以應寶夤。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Fengxian rebelled in Zhengping and Xue Xiuyi gathered forces in Hedong, seizing the salt pools and besieging Puban, east and west linking to answer Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengxian rebelled in Zhengping; Xue Xiuyi massed in Hedong, seized the salt pools, besieged Puban, and linked east and west with Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 承業乃據河東。

translations.literal: Chengye then held Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye held Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時有詔廢鹽池稅，承業上表曰：「鹽池天資賄貨，密邇京畿，唯須寶而護之，均贍以理。

translations.literal: There was an edict abolishing the salt-pool tax; Chengye memorialized, "The salt pools are Heaven's gift of wealth, close to the capital—only treasure and guard them and share out by rule.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the salt tax; Chengye memorialized: "The salt pools are Heaven's wealth, hard by the capital—they must be treasured, guarded, and fairly shared.

sentences.zh: 今四境多虞，府藏罄竭，然冀、定二州，且亡且亂，常調之絹，不復可收。

translations.literal: Now on four sides there are many alarms and the treasury is empty; yet Ji and Ding provinces are perishing in disorder and their regular silk levies can no longer be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Now alarms ring on every side and the treasury is bare; Ji and Ding are dying in chaos and their silk dues cannot be gathered.

sentences.zh: 仰惟府庫，有出無入，必須經綸，出入相補。

translations.literal: Looking up at the storehouses, outflow without inflow—balance must be managed, out and in must aid each other.
translations.idiomatic: The coffers spend without receiving—accounts must be balanced, outgo matched by income.

sentences.zh: 略論鹽稅，一年之中，准絹而言，猶不應減三十萬疋也。

translations.literal: Roughly speaking, in one year the salt tax, measured in silk, should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In one year the salt levy, reckoned in silk, should not fall below three hundred thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 便是移冀、定二州置於畿甸，今若廢之，事同再失。

translations.literal: That is like placing Ji and Ding within the capital domain; to abolish it now is to lose twice over.
translations.idiomatic: That is like keeping Ji and Ding within the royal domain; to abolish it now is double loss.

sentences.zh: 臣前仰違嚴旨，不先討關賊，徑解河東者，非是閑長安而急蒲阪。

translations.literal: Your servant earlier disobeyed the stern order and did not first attack the border rebels but went straight to relieve Hedong—not because he cared little for Chang'an and hurried to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: I earlier defied the stern order and did not strike the border rebels first but relieved Hedong—not because I slighted Chang'an and rushed to Puban.

sentences.zh: 蒲阪一陷，沒失鹽池，三軍口命，濟贍理絕。

translations.literal: Once Puban fell the salt pools would be lost and the three armies' mouths would have no provision—the means of crossing would be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Once Puban fell the salt pools were lost and the armies' mouths had no supply—the lifeline was cut.

sentences.zh: 天助大魏，茲計不爽。

translations.literal: Heaven aided Great Wei and this plan did not miss.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aided Great Wei and the plan held.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖升平之年，無所乏少，猶創置鹽官而加典護。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's years of peace there was no lack, yet he still created salt officials and added guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Gaozu's peaceful years, when want was unknown, he set salt officers and guardians.

sentences.zh: 非為物而競利，恐由利而亂俗也。

translations.literal: It was not for goods to compete for profit but fearing that from profit custom would be corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Not to wring profit from goods but lest profit corrupt custom.

sentences.zh: 況今王公素餐，百官屍祿，租徵六年之粟，調折來歲之資。

translations.literal: Moreover today princes and dukes eat salary without service and officials hold post without work; rent is levied for six years' grain and corvée mulcts next year's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Today lords feast without serving and officers draw pay without labor; rent takes six years' grain and corvée eats next year's stock.

sentences.zh: 此皆出入私財，奪人膂力，豈是願言，事不獲已。

translations.literal: All this is private outlay seizing men's strength—not what we wish, but what we cannot avoid.
translations.idiomatic: All is private spending of public muscle—not our wish but our bind.

sentences.zh: 臣輒符司監將尉，還率所部，依常收稅，更聽後敕。

translations.literal: Your servant has ordered the supervising office and the commandant to return with their commands and resume regular collection, awaiting further edict.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered the supervising office and commandant to return with their troops and collect the tax as usual, pending further command.

sentences.zh: 」及雍州平，除雍州刺史。

translations.literal: " When Yong Province was pacified he was made Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yong was pacified he was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，封上党王，尋改馮翊王，後降為郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang, soon changed to Prince of Fengyi, later reduced to Commandery Duke.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession he was Prince of Shangdang, soon Prince of Fengyi, later demoted to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，加侍中、兼尚書令、大行台，仍鎮長安。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of the Ministry of Works, added Palace Attendant, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Secretariat, and still garrisoned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became Duke of Works, Palace Attendant, Concurrent Director and Grand Secretariat, still holding Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 節閔立，遷太尉公、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Jiemin was enthroned he was transferred to Duke of the Grand Commandant and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiemin succeeded he was Grand Commandant and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之敗，斛斯椿先據河橋，謀誅爾硃。

translations.literal: After defeat at Hanling, Husijun first held Heyang Bridge and plotted to kill Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Hanling, Husijun seized Heyang Bridge and plotted to kill the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 使承業入洛，啟節閔誅世隆兄弟之意。

translations.literal: Chengye was sent into Luoyang to inform Jiemin of the intent to execute Shilong and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye was sent to Luoyang to tell Jiemin of the plan to kill Shilong and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，轉太傅，以定策功，更封開國子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he was transferred to Grand Tutor; for settling the succession he was further enfeoffed Baron of the Opening State.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession he was Grand Tutor; for fixing the succession he was further enfeoffed Baron of the Opening State.

sentences.zh: 承業表請回授其姨兄廷尉卿元洪超次子惲。

translations.literal: Chengye memorialized asking that the enfeoffment be transferred to his maternal cousin's son, the Vice Director of the Court for Ceremonials Yuan Hongchao's second son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to transfer the enfeoffment to his cousin's son Yun, second son of Vice Director Yuan Hongchao.

sentences.zh: 初，承業生而母亡，為洪超母所撫養，是以求讓。

translations.literal: At first Chengye's mother died at his birth and he was raised by Hongchao's mother; hence the request to yield.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at his birth; Hongchao's mother raised him—hence the request.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: It was granted.

sentences.zh: 武帝入關，承業時鎮武牢，亦隨赴長安，位太師、錄尚書事，封上党王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes Chengye was then garrisoning Wulao; he also followed to Chang'an, held office as Grand Preceptor and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing, and was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes Chengye held Wulao and followed to Chang'an as Grand Preceptor, recording affairs, and Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，薨，贈假黃鉞、大丞相、都督三十州諸軍事、雍州刺史，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he died; he was posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Chancellor, commander of thirty provinces' military affairs and Governor of Yong, posthumous name Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he died, posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Chancellor, commander of thirty provinces and Governor of Yong, posthumous name Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 承業少輕俠，鬥雞走馬，力爭殺人，因亡抵龍門將陳興德家。

translations.literal: In youth Chengye was light and chivalrous, cockfighting and racing horses, striving in killings; he fled and reached the house of Chen Xingde, garrison commander at Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Chengye was rakish—cockfights, horses, brawls that killed—and fled to Longmen garrison commander Chen Xingde.

sentences.zh: 會赦，乃免。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 因以後妻羅前夫女呂氏妻興德兄興恩以報之。

translations.literal: He therefore gave his stepwife Luo's daughter by her former husband, the Lü clan, in marriage to Xingde's elder brother Xingen in return.
translations.idiomatic: He married his stepmother Luo's stepdaughter, a Lü, to Xingde's brother Xingen in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 羅年大承業十餘歲，酷妒忌。

translations.literal: Luo was more than ten years older than Chengye and fiercely jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was more than ten years Chengye's senior and fiercely jealous.

sentences.zh: 承業雅相敬愛，無姬妾。

translations.literal: Chengye still respected and loved her deeply and kept no concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye still honored and loved her and kept no concubines.

sentences.zh: 童侍之中在承業左右嫌疑致死者，乃有數四。

translations.literal: Among boy attendants at Chengye's side, those suspected and put to death numbered several.
translations.idiomatic: Several boy attendants at his side were suspected and killed.

sentences.zh: 前妻張氏二子，子彥、子裕。

translations.literal: His first wife Lady Zhang had two sons, Ziyan and Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: His first wife Lady Zhang bore Ziyan and Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 羅生三子：紹遠、士亮、季亮。

translations.literal: Luo bore three sons: Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo bore Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆雄武。

translations.literal: The brothers were all bold in war.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all fierce in battle.

sentences.zh: 子彥本名雋，有膂力，以累從父征討功，封槐里縣子。

translations.literal: Ziyan's original name was Jun; he had great strength and for repeated service in his father's campaigns was enfeoffed Baron of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan, originally Jun, was immensely strong; for repeated campaigns with his father he was Baron of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝與齊神武構隙，加子彥中軍大都督、行台僕射，鎮恆農，以為心膂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu fell out with Qi Shenwu, Ziyan was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and Vice Director of the Secretariat, garrisoning Hengnong as his trusted arm.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu quarreled with Qi Shenwu, Ziyan was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and Vice Director, garrisoning Hengnong as his right hand.

sentences.zh: 及從帝入關，封高平郡公，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor into the passes he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping and made Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor into the passes he was Duke of Gaoping and Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.

sentences.zh: 以從征竇泰、戰沙苑功，加開府、侍中。

translations.literal: For following the campaign against Dou Tai and fighting at Shayuan he was made Opening Office and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For campaigning against Dou Tai and fighting at Shayuan he was made Opening Office and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及東復舊京，以子彥兼尚書令、行司州牧，留鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: When the east was recovered and the old capital restored, Ziyan was made Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing and Acting Governor of Si Province, remaining to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the east was recovered he was Concurrent Director and Acting Governor of Si, left to hold Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後以不利，班師。

translations.literal: Later, because things went ill, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when affairs turned bad, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大統七年，拜太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong he was Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子彥少常墜馬折臂，肘上骨起寸餘。

translations.literal: Ziyan in youth had often fallen from his horse and broken his arm; the bone above the elbow rose more than an inch.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ziyan often fell and broke his arm; bone rose an inch above the elbow.

sentences.zh: 乃命開肉鋸骨，流血數升，言戲自若。

translations.literal: He then ordered the flesh cut open and the bone sawed; blood flowed in several sheng and he spoke as if in jest.
translations.idiomatic: He had the flesh opened and the bone sawed; blood poured in sheng yet he jested calmly.

sentences.zh: 時以為逾於關羽。

translations.literal: Men of the time thought him beyond Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His age thought him bolder than Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 末年石發，舉體生瘡，雖親戚兄弟以為惡疾。

translations.literal: In his last years stone eruptions broke out over his body; even kin thought it a foul disease.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years stony growths broke out; kin took it for a foul disease.

sentences.zh: 子彥曰：「惡疾如此，難以自明。

translations.literal: Ziyan said, "With a foul disease like this it is hard to prove oneself innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan said, "With such a disease I cannot prove my innocence.

sentences.zh: 世無良醫，吾其死矣！

translations.literal: There is no good physician in the world—I am as good as dead!
translations.idiomatic: There is no skilled doctor in the world—I am as good as dead!

sentences.zh: 嘗聞惡疾蝮蛇螫之不痛，試為求之，當令兄弟知我。

translations.literal: I have heard that with foul disease a viper's sting does not hurt—let us try to find one so my brothers may know me.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that with this disease a viper's bite does not hurt—let us find one so my brothers know I am myself.

sentences.zh: 」及于南山得蛇，以股觸之，痛楚號叫，俄而腫死。

translations.literal: " When they got a snake on South Mountain he touched it to his thigh; he cried out in pain and soon the swelling died.
translations.idiomatic: " They found a snake on South Mountain; he touched it to his thigh, cried in pain, and the swelling soon subsided.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of it.

sentences.zh: 慟哭曰：「失我良將！

translations.literal: He mourned and said, "I have lost my good general!
translations.idiomatic: He wept and said, "I have lost my fine general!

sentences.zh: 」贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously made Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously made Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 子裕位衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Ziyu held office as Vice Director of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was Vice Director of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 啟舍凡階十七級，為子義貞求官。

translations.literal: He memorialized giving up seventeen ordinary ranks of salary to seek office for his son Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He gave up seventeen ranks of ordinary salary to seek office for his son Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 除左將軍，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yizhen was made Left General and added Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was made Left General and Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 又以父勳，封平原縣伯。

translations.literal: Again for his father's merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's merit he was also Baron of Pingyuan.
