sentences.zh: 義貞弟兕，字若汗。

translations.literal: Yizhen's younger brother Si, style name Ruohan.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen's younger brother Si, styled Ruohan.

sentences.zh: 性機辯，強記博聞，雅重賓游，尤善談論。

translations.literal: By nature quick-witted and eloquent, with a strong memory and wide learning; he valued guests and companions and excelled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and eloquent, with a formidable memory and wide learning, he cherished guests and companions and excelled in debate.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武西遷，別封鄴縣侯。

translations.literal: When he followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward in the migration, he was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration and was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.

sentences.zh: 周天和初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianhe era of Zhou, he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Director with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhou's Tianhe era he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the ceremonial standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 曆熊、絳二州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served as governor of Xiong and Jiang provinces in succession, and in both posts earned a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xiong and Jiang in turn, winning a name for competence in each.

sentences.zh: 襲爵平原縣公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the ducal title of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，子熾嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Chi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Chi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 幼曾孫熾

translations.literal: Chi, great-grandson of You
translations.idiomatic: Chi, a great-grandson of You

sentences.zh: 熾字仲光，性敏慧，美姿容，頗涉群書，兼長武藝。

translations.literal: Chi, styled Zhongguang, was clever and quick, handsome in bearing, had read widely among the classics, and was also skilled in martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, styled Zhongguang, was clever and handsome, had dipped into many books, and was skilled in arms as well.

sentences.zh: 建德初，周武帝崇尚道法，求學兼經史者為通道館學士，熾應其選。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiande era, Emperor Wu of Zhou, honoring the Way, sought men versed in both the classics and histories to serve as scholars of the Passage Hall; Chi was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou, at the start of Jiande, sought scholars versed in classics and histories for the Passage Hall, Chi was among those chosen.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，自禦正上士擢為丞相府功曹參軍，加大都督，封陽平縣子，遷稍伯下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was prime minister, he was raised from Superior Gentleman of the Imperial Rectitude to Merit Officer in the Chancellor's Office, given the grand commandant rank, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangping, and moved to Junior Grand Master of the Lesser Earl.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was still prime minister, Chi rose from Superior Gentleman of the Imperial Rectitude to merit officer in the chancellor's office, was made grand commandant, enfeoffed Viscount of Yangping, and promoted to junior grand master of the lesser earl.

sentences.zh: 以平王謙，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: For suppressing Prince of Qi Wang Qian, he was awarded the ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For helping crush Wang Qian, Prince of Qi, he received the ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，熾率官屬先入清宮，即授內史舍人、上儀同三司，攝東宮右庶子，出入兩宮，甚被委遇。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, Chi led the officials in first entering the cleared palace; he was at once made Palace Attendant of the Inner Secretariat and superior ceremonial peer of the Three Excellencies, acting as Right Vice Heir Apparent of the Eastern Palace, moving in and out of both palaces and greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Sui, Chi led the officials into the cleared palace first and was made palace attendant of the inner secretariat with superior ceremonial rank, acting right vice heir apparent of the eastern palace—trusted in both courts.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿，改封饒陽縣子，進位開府儀同三司，改授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, his fief changed to Viscount of Raoyang, advanced to Director with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of ceremonies, had his fief changed to Raoyang, was given director's ceremonial rank, and became vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 大業中，歷位大理卿、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he held the posts of Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daye he served in turn as minister of justice and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾寇張掖，令熾擊之，追至青海，以功授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun raided Zhangye, Chi was ordered to strike them and pursued them to Qinghai; for his merit he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided Zhangye, Chi pursued them to Qinghai and, for his merit, was made grand master of splendid brightness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝幸江都宮，留熾東都居守，攝左候衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor visited the Jiangdu Palace and left Chi at the eastern capital as commandant, acting as Left Commander of the Waiting Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the emperor went to the Jiangdu palace and left Chi at the eastern capital as commandant, acting left commander of the waiting guard.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 子安世，通事謁者。

translations.literal: His son Anshi was an attendant for miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi served as attendant for miscellaneous matters.

sentences.zh: 熾弟晟。

translations.literal: Sheng, younger brother of Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Chi had a younger brother, Sheng.

sentences.zh: 熾弟晟

translations.literal: Sheng, younger brother of Chi
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, younger brother of Chi

sentences.zh: 晟字季晟，性通敏，略涉書記，善彈工射，矯捷過人。

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Jisheng, was quick and penetrating by nature, had dipped into written records, was skilled at archery and shooting, and was more agile than other men.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, styled Jisheng, was quick and keen, had some schooling, excelled at archery, and moved with uncanny agility.

sentences.zh: 年十八，仕周為司衛上士。

translations.literal: At eighteen he entered Zhou's service as Superior Gentleman of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered Zhou's service as superior gentleman of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 初未知名，唯隋文帝一見深異焉，謂曰：「長孫武藝逸群，又多奇略。

translations.literal: At first he was not yet known; only Emperor Wen of Sui, on a single meeting, was deeply struck and said to him:
translations.idiomatic: At first he was unknown—until Emperor Wen of Sui met him once and was deeply struck, saying:

sentences.zh: 後之名將，非此子邪？

translations.literal: "Changsun's martial skill surpasses the crowd, and he has many singular stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: "Changsun's martial skill surpasses the crowd, and he holds many singular stratagems.

sentences.zh: 」及突厥攝圖請婚，周以趙王招女妻之。

translations.literal: The famous general of later days—will it not be this man?"
translations.idiomatic: The famous general of later days—will it not be this man?"

sentences.zh: 周與攝圖各相誇競，妙選驍勇以充使者，因遣晟副汝南公宇文神慶送千金公主至其牙。

translations.literal: When the Türk Qaghan Shetu sought marriage, Zhou gave him the daughter of Prince Zhao of Zhao as wife.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk qaghan Shetu sought a marriage alliance, Zhou gave him the daughter of Prince Zhao.

sentences.zh: 前後使人數十輩，攝圖多不禮之，獨愛晟，每共遊獵，留之竟歲。

translations.literal: Zhou and Shetu each boasted against the other and chose the finest warriors to serve as envoys; Sheng was therefore sent as deputy to the Duke of Runan, Yuwen Shenqing, to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Shetu each boasted their valor and picked the finest warriors as envoys; Sheng was sent as deputy to Duke of Runan Yuwen Shenqing to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to Shetu's camp.

sentences.zh: 嘗有二雕，飛而爭肉，因以箭兩隻與晟，請射取之。

translations.literal: Envoys before and after numbered several tens; Shetu was mostly discourteous to them, but he alone favored Sheng, hunted with him constantly, and kept him a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of envoys came and went; Shetu treated most discourteously, but favored Sheng alone, hunted with him constantly, and kept him a full year.

sentences.zh: 晟馳往，遇雕相玃，遂一發雙貫焉。

translations.literal: Once two eagles flew up fighting over meat; he therefore gave Sheng two arrows and asked him to shoot them down.
translations.idiomatic: Once two eagles fought in the air over meat; Shetu gave Sheng two arrows and asked him to bring them down.

sentences.zh: 攝圖喜，命諸子弟貴人皆相親友，冀昵近之，以學彈射。

translations.literal: Sheng galloped up; when he met the eagles grappling each other, he loosed one shaft and pierced both.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng galloped up, found the eagles locked together, and dropped them both with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 其弟處羅侯號突利設，尤得眾心，為攝圖所忌，密托心腹，陰與晟盟。

translations.literal: Shetu was pleased and ordered all his younger kinsmen and nobles to befriend Sheng, hoping to draw near him and learn archery.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Shetu had his younger kinsmen and nobles befriend Sheng so they might learn archery from him.

sentences.zh: 晟與之遊獵，因察山川形勢，部眾強弱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli She, was especially beloved by the people and was envied by Shetu; he secretly entrusted his heart to Sheng and secretly allied with him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli She, was especially beloved by the people and envied by Shetu; he secretly entrusted himself to Sheng and made a hidden alliance.

sentences.zh: 皆盡知之。

translations.literal: Sheng hunted with him and thereby surveyed the mountains and rivers, the terrain, and the strength of the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng hunted with him and surveyed mountains, rivers, terrain, and tribal strength.

sentences.zh: 還，拜奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He came to know them all thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He came to know them all thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，攝圖曰：「我，周家親也。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made commandant of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 今隋公自立而不能制，何面目見可賀敦！

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said:
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang's first year Shetu said:

sentences.zh: 」因與高寶寧攻陷臨渝鎮，約諸面部落，謀共南侵。

translations.literal: "I am kin to the house of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: "I am kin to the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 文帝新立，由是大懼，修長城，發兵屯北境。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot control him—what face have I to show the kehuden!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot control him—what face have I to show the kehuden!"

sentences.zh: 命陰壽鎮幽州、虞慶則鎮并州，屯兵為之備。

translations.literal: He therefore joined Gao Baoning in attacking and taking Linyu Fort, rallied the tribal chiefs of the various divisions, and plotted a joint southern invasion.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Gao Baoning in taking Linyu Fort, rallied the tribal chiefs, and plotted a joint invasion of the south.

sentences.zh: 晟先知攝圖、玷厥、阿波、突利等叔侄兄弟各統強兵，俱號可汗，分居四面，內懷猜忌，外示和同，難以力征，易可離間。

translations.literal: The emperor had newly taken the throne and was therefore greatly afraid; he repaired the Long Wall and sent troops to garrison the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had only just taken the throne and was greatly alarmed; he repaired the Long Wall and sent troops to the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 因上書曰：「臣於周末，忝充外使，匈奴倚伏，實所具知。

translations.literal: He ordered Yin Shou to garrison Youzhou and Yu Qingze to garrison Bingzhou, stationing troops as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yin Shou to hold Youzhou and Yu Qingze to hold Bingzhou, with troops stationed as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 玷厥之於攝圖，兵強而位下，外名相屬，內隙已彰，鼓動其情，必將自戰。

translations.literal: Sheng had long known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and other uncles, nephews, and brothers each commanded strong armies, all styled qaghan, holding the four quarters—harboring suspicion within while showing harmony without—hard to conquer by force, easy to sunder by division.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had long known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and other uncles and brothers each commanded strong armies, all styled qaghan and holding the four quarters—suspicious within, harmonious without—hard to conquer by force, easy to split by intrigue.

sentences.zh: 又處羅侯者，攝圖之弟，奸多而勢弱，曲取眾心，國人愛之，因為攝圖所忌。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized:

sentences.zh: 又阿波首鼠，介在其間，頗畏攝圖，受其牽率，唯強是與，未有定心。

translations.literal: "Your servant, at the end of Zhou, was honored to serve as envoy abroad; the Türks' rises and falls are what I know in detail.
translations.idiomatic: "At the end of Zhou your servant was honored to serve abroad; the Türks' rises and falls I know in detail.

sentences.zh: 宜遠交而近攻，離強而合弱。

translations.literal: Dianjue toward Shetu has the stronger army but the lower rank; outwardly they are joined in name, but inwardly the rift is already plain—if their passions are stirred, they will surely fight each other.
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue toward Shetu has the stronger army but the lower rank; joined in name outwardly, their rift is already plain—stir their passions and they will fight each other.

sentences.zh: 通使玷厥，說合阿波，則攝圖回兵，自防右地。

translations.literal: Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning and numerous in followers but weak in power; he curries the people's hearts and the nation loves him, and therefore Shetu envies him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning, weak in power, beloved of the people, and therefore envied by Shetu.

sentences.zh: 又引處羅，遣連奚、嵆，則攝圖分眾，還備左方。

translations.literal: Abo is irresolute, caught between them; he fears Shetu much, is pulled along by him, follows only the strong, and has no settled heart.
translations.idiomatic: Abo wavers between them, fears Shetu, is pulled along by him, follows only the strong, and has no settled heart.

sentences.zh: 道尾猜嫌，腹心離阻，十數年後，承釁討之，必可一舉而空其國。」

translations.literal: One should befriend the distant and attack the near, divide the strong and unite the weak.
translations.idiomatic: Befriend the distant, attack the near; divide the strong, unite the weak.

sentences.zh: 上省表大悅，因召與語。

translations.literal: Send envoys to Dianjue and persuade Abo to join him, and Shetu will turn his army to guard the western lands himself.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to Dianjue and win Abo to him, and Shetu will turn his army to guard the west himself.

sentences.zh: 晟口陳形勢，手畫山川，寫其虛實，皆如指掌。

translations.literal: Also draw in Chuluohou and send him to link with Xi and Qi, and Shetu will divide his host and return to guard the eastern quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Draw in Chuluohou and link him with Xi and Qi, and Shetu will divide his host to guard the east.

sentences.zh: 上深嗟異，皆納用焉。

translations.literal: Suspicion at the tail, estrangement at the heart—after a dozen years or so, strike when the chance appears, and in one move you may empty their state."
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion at the tail, estrangement at the heart—after a dozen years strike when chance appears, and in one move you may empty their state."

sentences.zh: 因遣太僕元暉出伊吾道，使詣玷厥，賜以狼頭纛，謬為欽敬。

translations.literal: The emperor, on reading the memorial, was greatly pleased and summoned him to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with delight and summoned him to speak.

sentences.zh: 玷厥使來，引居攝圖使上。

translations.literal: Sheng set forth the situation with his mouth and drew the mountains and rivers with his hand, writing out their strengths and weaknesses as if they lay in his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng described the situation aloud and sketched mountains and rivers with his hand, laying out strength and weakness as if on his palm.

sentences.zh: 反間既行，果相猜貳。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in deep admiration and adopted it all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and adopted it all.

sentences.zh: 授晟車騎將軍，出黃龍道，齎敝賜奚、嵆、契丹等，遣為鄉導，得至處羅侯所，深布心腹，誘令內附。

translations.literal: He therefore sent the Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu route with envoys to Dianjue, bestowing a wolf-head banner and falsely showing deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu route to Dianjue with a wolf-head banner and feigned deep respect.

sentences.zh: 二年，攝圖號四十萬騎，自蘭州入，至於周盤，破達奚長儒軍。

translations.literal: When Dianjue's envoy came, he was lodged above Shetu's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Dianjue's envoy arrived, he was lodged above Shetu's envoy.

sentences.zh: 更欲南入，玷厥不從，引兵而去。

translations.literal: Once the stratagem of division was set in motion, they truly became mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Once the stratagem of division was set in motion, they truly became mutually suspicious.

sentences.zh: 時晟又說染幹詐告攝圖曰：「鐵勒等反，欲襲其牙。

translations.literal: Sheng was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and sent out by the Yellow Dragon route, bearing worn gifts for Xi, Qi, Khitan, and others, sent as guides, and reached Chuluohou's camp, where he laid out his inner thoughts deeply and enticed him to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was made general of chariots and cavalry and sent by the Yellow Dragon route with worn gifts for Xi, Qi, Khitan, and others as guides; he reached Chuluohou, won his confidence, and enticed him to submit.

sentences.zh: 」攝圖乃懼，回兵出塞。

translations.literal: In the second year Shetu, styled at four hundred thousand horsemen, entered from Lanzhou as far as Zhoupan and broke the army of Daxi Changru.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Shetu, claiming four hundred thousand horsemen, entered from Lanzhou to Zhoupan and broke Daxi Changru's army.

sentences.zh: 後數年，突厥大入，發八道元帥出拒之。

translations.literal: He wished to press farther south, but Dianjue would not follow and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to press farther south, but Dianjue refused and led his troops away.

sentences.zh: 阿波至涼州，與竇榮定戰，賊帥累北。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng also persuaded Ran'gan to falsely report to Shetu:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sheng also persuaded Ran'gan to falsely report to Shetu:

sentences.zh: 時晟為偏將，使謂之曰：「攝圖每來，戰皆大勝。

translations.literal: "The Tiele and others have rebelled and mean to strike your camp."
translations.idiomatic: "The Tiele and others have rebelled and mean to strike your camp."

sentences.zh: 阿波才入，便即致敗，此乃突厥之恥。

translations.literal: Shetu was therefore afraid and turned his army back beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu was afraid and turned his army back beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 且攝圖之與阿波，兵勢本敵，今攝圖日勝，為眾所崇，阿波不利，為國生辱。

translations.literal: Several years later the Türks invaded in force; eight route marshals were sent out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the Türks invaded in force and eight route marshals were sent to resist.

sentences.zh: 攝圖必當因此以罪歸於阿波，成其夙計，滅北牙矣。

translations.literal: Abo reached Liangzhou and fought Dou Rongding; the enemy leaders were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Abo reached Liangzhou and fought Dou Rongding; the enemy leaders were repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 」阿波使至，晟又謂曰：「今達頭與隋連和，而攝圖不能制。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng was a subordinate general and sent word to him:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sheng was a subordinate general and sent word to him:

sentences.zh: 可汗何不依附天子，連結達頭，相合為強？

translations.literal: "Whenever Shetu comes, battle always ends in great victory.
translations.idiomatic: "Whenever Shetu comes, battle always ends in great victory.

sentences.zh: 此萬全之計。

translations.literal: Abo has only just entered and at once suffers defeat—this is the Türks' shame.
translations.idiomatic: Abo has only just entered and at once suffers defeat—this is the Türks' shame.

sentences.zh: 豈若喪兵負罪，歸就攝圖，受其戮辱耶！

translations.literal: Moreover Shetu and Abo were originally equal in military strength; now Shetu wins day by day and is exalted by the masses, while Abo fares ill and brings disgrace on the state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shetu and Abo were originally equal in strength; now Shetu wins day by day and is exalted by the masses, while Abo fares ill and brings disgrace on the state.

sentences.zh: 」阿波納之，因留塞上。

translations.literal: Shetu will surely use this to lay the blame on Abo and accomplish his long-held plan to destroy the northern camp."
translations.idiomatic: Shetu will surely use this to lay the blame on Abo and accomplish his long-held plan to destroy the northern camp."

sentences.zh: 後使人隨晟入朝。

translations.literal: When Abo's envoy arrived, Sheng also said to him:
translations.idiomatic: When Abo's envoy arrived, Sheng also said to him:

sentences.zh: 時攝圖與衛王軍遇，戰于白道，敗走。

translations.literal: "Now Datou is allied with Sui, and Shetu cannot control him.
translations.idiomatic: "Now Datou is allied with Sui, and Shetu cannot control him.

sentences.zh: 至磧，聞阿波懷貳，乃掩北牙，盡獲其眾而殺其母。

translations.literal: Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven, join with Datou, and combine into strength?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven, join with Datou, and combine into strength?

sentences.zh: 阿波還無所歸。

translations.literal: This is the plan of perfect safety.
translations.idiomatic: This is the plan of perfect safety.

sentences.zh: 西奔玷厥，乞師十餘萬，東擊攝圖，復得故地。

translations.literal: Will you rather lose your army, bear guilt, return to Shetu, and suffer his slaughter and humiliation!"
translations.idiomatic: Will you rather lose your army, bear guilt, return to Shetu, and suffer his slaughter and humiliation!"

sentences.zh: 收散卒，與攝圖相攻。

translations.literal: Abo accepted this and therefore remained beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Abo accepted this and remained beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 阿波頻勝，其勢益強。

translations.literal: Abo won repeatedly and his power grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Abo won again and again, and his power grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 攝圖又遣使朝貢，公主自請改姓，乞為帝女，上許之。

translations.literal: Shetu again sent envoys with tribute; the princess herself asked to change her surname and begged to be made the emperor's daughter, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu again sent tribute; the princess asked to take the emperor's surname and become his daughter, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣晟副虞慶則使於攝圖，賜公主姓為楊氏，改封大義公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sheng was sent as deputy to Yu Qingze on a mission to Shetu; the princess was given the surname Yang and her fief changed to Princess of Great Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Sheng went as deputy to Yu Qingze to Shetu; the princess was given the surname Yang and enfeoffed as Princess of Great Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 攝圖奉詔，不肯起拜。

translations.literal: Shetu received the edict but refused to rise and bow.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu received the edict but refused to rise and bow.

sentences.zh: 晟進曰：「突厥與隋俱是大國天子，可汗不起，安敢違意。

translations.literal: Sheng advanced and said:
translations.idiomatic: Sheng stepped forward and said:

sentences.zh: 但可賀敦為帝女，則可汗是大隋女媚，奈何不敬婦公？

translations.literal: "Türks and Sui are both great states of the Son of Heaven; if the qaghan does not rise, how dare I disobey his will.
translations.idiomatic: "Türks and Sui are both great powers of the Son of Heaven; if the qaghan does not rise, how dare I disobey his will.

sentences.zh: 」攝圖笑謂其達官曰：「須拜婦公。

translations.literal: But the kehuden is the emperor's daughter—then the qaghan is the great son-in-law of Great Sui; how can he fail to respect his wife's father-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: But the kehuden is the emperor's daughter—then the qaghan is Great Sui's son-in-law; how can he fail to respect his wife's father-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 」乃拜受詔。

translations.literal: Shetu laughed and said to his nobles, "One must bow to the wife's father-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Shetu laughed and told his nobles, "One must bow to the wife's father-in-law."

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，授儀同三司、左勳衛車騎將軍。

translations.literal: He then bowed and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then bowed and received the edict.

sentences.zh: 七年，攝圖死，遣晟持節拜其弟處羅侯為莫何可汗，以其子雍閭為葉護可汗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was sent bearing credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Mohe Qaghan and his son Yonglu as Yehu Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was sent with credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Mohe Qaghan and his son Yonglu as Yehu Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 處羅侯因晟奏曰：「阿波為天所滅，與五六千騎在山谷間，當取之以獻。

translations.literal: Chuluohou, through Sheng, memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou, through Sheng, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 」時召文武議焉。

translations.literal: "Abo was destroyed by Heaven and is in the mountain valleys with five or six thousand horsemen—he should be taken and presented."
translations.idiomatic: "Abo was destroyed by Heaven and is in the mountain valleys with five or six thousand horsemen—he should be taken and presented."

sentences.zh: 樂安西元諧曰：「請就彼梟首，以懲其惡。

translations.literal: At that time civil and military officials were summoned to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were summoned to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 」武陽公李充請生將入朝，顯戮而示百姓。

translations.literal: Yue'an Xi Yuanxie of the Western Regions said:
translations.idiomatic: Yue'an Xi Yuanxie of the Western Regions said:

sentences.zh: 上問晟，晟曰：「阿波之惡，非負國家。

translations.literal: "Please go there and take his head to punish his wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: "Please go there and take his head to punish his wickedness."

sentences.zh: 因其困窮，取而為戮，恐非招遠之道。

translations.literal: Duke of Wuyang Li Chong asked to bring him alive into court and display the execution to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wuyang Li Chong asked to bring him alive into court and display the execution to the people.

sentences.zh: 不如兩存之。

translations.literal: Better to let both survive."
translations.idiomatic: Better to let both survive."

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 八年，處羅侯死，遣晟往吊，仍齎陳國所獻寶器，以賜雍閭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to offer condolences and also bore treasure vessels presented by Chen to bestow on Yonglu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to mourn him and bore treasure vessels Chen had presented, to bestow on Yonglu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，流人楊欽亡入突厥，詐言彭國公劉昶共宇文氏女謀欲反隋，遣其來密告公主。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the exiled Yang Qin fled into the Türks and falsely said that Duke of Peng Liu Chang together with a daughter of the Yuwen clan plotted rebellion against Sui, sending him to secretly inform the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the exile Yang Qin fled to the Türks and falsely claimed that Duke of Peng Liu Chang and a Yuwen daughter plotted against Sui, sending him to secretly inform the princess.

sentences.zh: 雍閭信之，乃不修貢。

translations.literal: Yonglu believed it and therefore ceased paying tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu believed it and stopped sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 又遣晟出使，微觀察焉。

translations.literal: Sheng was again sent on mission to observe subtly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was again sent on mission to observe subtly.

sentences.zh: 公主見晟，言辭不遜，又遣所私胡人安遂迦共欽計議，扇惑雍閭。

translations.literal: The princess saw Sheng with insolent speech and also sent her private Türk An Suijia together with Qin to plot, stirring Yonglu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess saw Sheng with insolent speech and also sent her private Turk An Suijia with Qin to plot, stirring Yonglu.

sentences.zh: 晟還，以狀奏。

translations.literal: Sheng returned and memorialized the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng returned and memorialized the facts.

sentences.zh: 又遣晟往索欽，雍閭欲勿與，謬曰：「客內無此色人。

translations.literal: He again sent Sheng to demand Qin; Yonglu wished not to hand him over and lied, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Sheng to demand Qin; Yonglu wished to withhold him and lied, saying:

sentences.zh: 」晟乃貨其達官，知欽所在，夜掩獲之，以示雍閭。

translations.literal: "Among the guests within there is no man of this complexion."
translations.idiomatic: "Among the guests within there is no man of this complexion."

sentences.zh: 因發公主私事。

translations.literal: Sheng then bribed his nobles, learned where Qin was, seized him by night in a surprise raid, and showed him to Yonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng bribed his nobles, learned where Qin was, seized him in a night raid, and showed him to Yonglu.

sentences.zh: 國人大恥。

translations.literal: He thereby exposed the princess's private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby exposed the princess's private affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍閭執遂迦等，並以付晟。

translations.literal: The nation was greatly shamed.
translations.idiomatic: The nation was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 使還，上大喜，加授開府，仍遣入蕃，涖殺大義公主。

translations.literal: Yonglu seized Ansuijia and the others and handed them all over to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu seized Ansuijia and the others and handed them all to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 雍閭又表請婚，僉議將許之。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the emperor was greatly pleased, advanced him to Director, and again sent him into the Türk lands to oversee the execution of the Princess of Great Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the emperor was greatly pleased, made him Director, and again sent him into the Türk lands to oversee the killing of the Princess of Great Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 晟奏曰：「臣觀雍閭反覆無信，特共玷厥有隙，所以依倚國家。

translations.literal: Yonglu again memorialized requesting marriage; the assembly deliberated and was about to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu again asked to marry; the assembly was about to grant it.

sentences.zh: 縱與為婚，終當必叛。

translations.literal: Sheng memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized:

sentences.zh: 今若得尚公主，承藉威靈，玷厥、染幹必又受其徵發。

translations.literal: "Your servant observes that Yonglu is fickle and faithless; he relies on the state only because he has a rift with Dianjue.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant observes that Yonglu is fickle and faithless; he relies on the state only because he has a rift with Dianjue.

sentences.zh: 強而更反，後恐難圖。

translations.literal: Even if a marriage is granted, he will surely rebel in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a marriage is granted, he will surely rebel in the end.

sentences.zh: 且染幹者，處羅侯之子，素有誠款，於今兩世。

translations.literal: If he now obtains an imperial princess and borrows her authority, Dianjue and Ran'gan will again suffer his summons to war.
translations.idiomatic: If he now obtains an imperial princess and borrows her authority, Dianjue and Ran'gan will again suffer his summons to war.

sentences.zh: 臣前與相見，亦乞通婚，不如許之，招令南徙。

translations.literal: Growing stronger, he will turn again—and later he may be hard to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Growing stronger, he will turn again—and later he may be hard to manage.

sentences.zh: 兵少力弱，易可撫馴，使敵雍閭，以為邊捍。

translations.literal: Moreover Ran'gan is the son of Chuluohou and has long shown sincere loyalty through two reigns now.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ran'gan is the son of Chuluohou and has long shown sincere loyalty through two reigns now.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: When I met him before, he too asked for marriage; better to grant it and summon him to move south.
translations.idiomatic: When I met him before, he too asked for marriage; better to grant it and summon him to move south.

sentences.zh: 」又遣慰喻染幹，許尚公主。

translations.literal: His troops are few and his power weak—easy to pacify and tame, set against Yonglu as a border shield.
translations.idiomatic: His troops are few and his power weak—easy to pacify and tame, set against Yonglu as a border shield.

sentences.zh: 十七年，染幹遣使隨晟來逆女。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 以宗女封安義公主以妻之。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to comfort and instruct Ran'gan and promised him an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent envoys to comfort Ran'gan and promised him an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 晟說染幹南徙，居度斤舊鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Ran'gan sent envoys with Sheng to receive the bride.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Ran'gan sent envoys with Sheng to receive the bride.

sentences.zh: 雍閭疾之，亟來抄略。

translations.literal: A clanswoman was enfeoffed as Princess of Anyi and given to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: A clanswoman was enfeoffed as Princess of Anyi and given to him as wife.

sentences.zh: 染幹伺知動靜，輒遣奏聞，是以賊來，每先有備。

translations.literal: Sheng persuaded Ran'gan to move south and dwell at the old seat of Dujin.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng persuaded Ran'gan to move south and dwell at the old seat of Dujin.

sentences.zh: 十九年，染幹因晟奏雍閭作攻具。

translations.literal: Yonglu resented this and repeatedly came to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu resented this and repeatedly came to raid.

sentences.zh: 欲打大同城。

translations.literal: Ran'gan watched for movements and at once sent memorials; therefore when bandits came he was always forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: Ran'gan watched for movements and at once sent memorials; therefore when bandits came he was always forewarned.

translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan.

translations.idiomatic: He died in his post; posthumously enfeoffed Pillar of State, posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 自喪初至及葬，明帝三臨之。

translations.literal: From the first of mourning until the burial, Emperor Ming thrice came in person.
translations.idiomatic: From the first of mourning until the burial, Emperor Ming thrice came in person.

sentences.zh: 典祀中大夫宇文容諫曰：「君臨臣喪，自有節制。

translations.literal: Director of Sacrifices Zhongdafu Yuwen Rong remonstrated: "The ruler attending a minister's mourning has its own measure.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Sacrifices Zhongdafu Yuwen Rong remonstrated: "The ruler attending a minister's mourning has its own measure.

sentences.zh: 今乘輿屢降，恐乖典禮。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage has repeatedly descended— I fear it strays from the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial carriage has repeatedly descended— I fear it strays from the canon.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not follow him.

sentences.zh: 其為上所追惜如此。

translations.literal: Such was the sovereign's mourning regret for him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the sovereign's mourning regret for him.

sentences.zh: 子嶸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 瓬弟禮，少以父任為散騎侍郎，與襄城公盧魯元等內侍。

translations.literal: Fang's younger brother Li, in youth through his father's appointment was Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, and with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and others served within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's younger brother Li, in youth through his father's appointment was Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, and with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and others served within the palace.

sentences.zh: 恭敏有才志。

translations.literal: Respectful, keen, and talented in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful, keen, and talented in purpose.

sentences.zh: 太武寵信之，曰：「其父親近吾祖，子在我左右，不亦宜乎。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu favored and trusted him, saying: "His father was close to my grandfather; the son at my side—is it not fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu favored and trusted him, saying: "His father was close to my grandfather; the son at my side—is it not fitting?"

sentences.zh: 長孫肥

translations.literal: Changsun Fei
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Fei

sentences.zh: 長孫肥，代人也。

translations.literal: Changsun Fei was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Fei was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，年十三，以選內侍。

translations.literal: In the time of Zhaocheng, at age thirteen he was chosen for inner attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Zhaocheng, at age thirteen he was chosen for inner attendance.

sentences.zh: 少有雅度，果毅少言。

translations.literal: In youth he had refined bearing, was resolute and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had refined bearing, was resolute and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 道武之在獨孤及賀蘭部，常侍從，禦侮左右，帝深信仗之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu was among the Dugu and Helan tribes, Fei constantly attended and followed, guarding against insult at his side; the emperor deeply trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu was among the Dugu and Helan tribes, Fei constantly attended and followed, guarding against insult at his side; the emperor deeply trusted and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與莫題等俱為大將，屢有軍功。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Mo Ti and others, were all great generals and repeatedly won military merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Mo Ti and others, were all great generals and repeatedly won military merit.

sentences.zh: 後從平中山，以功賜爵琅邪公。

translations.literal: Later he followed in the pacification of Zhongshan and for merit was granted the title Duke of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed in the pacification of Zhongshan and for merit was granted the title Duke of Langye.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿，改爵盧鄉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister Steward and his title changed to Marquis of Luxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister Steward and his title changed to Marquis of Luxiang.

sentences.zh: 時中山太守仇儒不樂內徙，亡匿趙郡，推趙准為主。

translations.literal: At that time the Administrator of Zhongshan, Qiu Ru, was unwilling to move inward; he fled and hid in Zhao commandery and set up Zhao Zhun as leader.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Administrator of Zhongshan, Qiu Ru, was unwilling to move inward; he fled and hid in Zhao commandery and set up Zhao Zhun as leader.

sentences.zh: 妄造妖言云：「燕東傾，趙當續。

translations.literal: He falsely made demonic words saying: "Yan tilts east; Zhao shall continue.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely made demonic words saying: "Yan tilts east; Zhao shall continue.

sentences.zh: 欲知其名，淮水不足。

translations.literal: If you wish to know his name, the Huai River is not enough.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to know his name, the Huai River is not enough.

sentences.zh: 」准喜而從之，自號钜鹿公，儒為長史。

translations.literal: " Zhun gladly followed him, styled himself Duke of Julu, and Ru served as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhun gladly followed him, styled himself Duke of Julu, and Ru served as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 據關城，連引丁零，殺害長吏。

translations.literal: They held Guan city, linked in the Dingling, and killed the chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: They held Guan city, linked in the Dingling, and killed the chief officials.

sentences.zh: 肥討破准於九門，斬仇儒，禽准。

translations.literal: Fei defeated Zhun at Jiumen, beheaded Qiu Ru, and captured Zhun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fei defeated Zhun at Jiumen, beheaded Qiu Ru, and captured Zhun alive.

sentences.zh: 詔以儒肉食准，傳送京師，轅之於市，夷其族。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Ru's flesh be used to feed Zhun; he was sent to the capital, broken on the wheel at the market, and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that Ru's flesh be used to feed Zhun; he was sent to the capital, broken on the wheel at the market, and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 除肥兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Fei was appointed Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was appointed Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 姚平之寇平陽，道武征肥與毗陵王順等為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Yao Ping raided Pingyang, Emperor Daowu campaigned and made Fei, with Prince of Piling Shun and others, the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Ping raided Pingyang, Emperor Daowu campaigned and made Fei, with Prince of Piling Shun and others, the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 平退保柴壁，帝進攻屠之。

translations.literal: Ping retreated to hold Chaiwall; the emperor advanced and stormed it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping retreated to hold Chaiwall; the emperor advanced and stormed it.

sentences.zh: 遣肥還鎮兗州，撫慰河南，威信著於淮泗。

translations.literal: He sent Fei back to garrison Yan Province and comfort Henan; his prestige and trust were manifest on the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fei back to garrison Yan Province and comfort Henan; his prestige and trust were manifest on the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 善策謀，勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: Skilled in stratagem, his courage topped the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in stratagem, his courage topped the generals.

sentences.zh: 前後征討，未嘗失敗。

translations.literal: In campaigns before and after, he never once failed.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns before and after, he never once failed.

sentences.zh: 故每有大難，令肥當之；

translations.literal: Therefore whenever there was great peril they put Fei in charge;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whenever there was great peril they put Fei in charge;

sentences.zh: 南平中原，西摧羌寇，肥功居多，賞賜千計。

translations.literal: in pacifying the central plains southward and crushing Qiang raiders westward, Fei's merit was greatest; rewards numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: in pacifying the central plains southward and crushing Qiang raiders westward, Fei's merit was greatest; rewards numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 後降爵藍田侯。

translations.literal: Later his title was reduced to Marquis of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was reduced to Marquis of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰武，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Wu, buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Wu, buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子翰襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Han succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 翰少有父風。

translations.literal: Han in youth had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Han in youth had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 道武時，以善騎射，為獵郎。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Daowu, for skill in mounted archery he was made Hunt Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daowu, for skill in mounted archery he was made Hunt Officer.

sentences.zh: 明元之在外，翰與元磨渾等潛謀奉迎。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan was abroad, Han with Yuan Mohun and others secretly plotted to welcome and install him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan was abroad, Han with Yuan Mohun and others secretly plotted to welcome and install him.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，與磨渾等拾遺左右。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, he and Mohun and others attended to remonstrance at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, he and Mohun and others attended to remonstrance at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷平南將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 率眾鎮北境，威名甚著。

translations.literal: He led troops to garrison the northern frontier; his martial renown was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to garrison the northern frontier; his martial renown was very great.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，封平陽王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀之入寇雲中，太武親征之。

translations.literal: When the Rouran khan Datan invaded Yunzhong, Emperor Taiwu campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran khan Datan invaded Yunzhong, Emperor Taiwu campaigned in person.

sentences.zh: 遣翰與東平公娥清出長川討大檀。

translations.literal: He sent Han with Duke of Dongping E Qing out of Changchuan to attack Datan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han with Duke of Dongping E Qing out of Changchuan to attack Datan.

sentences.zh: 大檀北遁，追擊克獲而還。

translations.literal: Datan fled north; they pursued, struck, captured booty, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Datan fled north; they pursued, struck, captured booty, and returned.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 從襲赫連昌，破之。

translations.literal: He followed in the assault on Helian Chang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the assault on Helian Chang and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 翰清正嚴明，喜撫將士，薨，太武為之流涕，親臨其喪。

translations.literal: Han was upright, pure, and strict and bright; he delighted in comforting officers and soldiers; when he died, Emperor Taiwu wept for him and came in person to his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Han was upright, pure, and strict and bright; he delighted in comforting officers and soldiers; when he died, Emperor Taiwu wept for him and came in person to his mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪禮依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: Mourning rites followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Wei, buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Wei, buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子成襲爵，降為公，位南部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Cheng succeeded to the title, reduced to duke, and held the post of Director of the Southern Department.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng succeeded to the title, reduced to duke, and held the post of Director of the Southern Department.

sentences.zh: 卒，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died, buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died, buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 翰弟陵，位駕部尚書。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Ling held the post of Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother Ling held the post of Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，好學愛士。

translations.literal: By nature generous and broad; he loved learning and cherished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: By nature generous and broad; he loved learning and cherished scholars.

sentences.zh: 封吳郡公，贈吳郡王。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Duke of Wu commandery, posthumously made Prince of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed Duke of Wu commandery, posthumously made Prince of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 諡恭，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Gong, buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Gong, buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昭成之末，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: Discussion says: At the end of Zhaocheng, the multitudes rebelled and kin turned away.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: At the end of Zhaocheng, subjects rebelled and kin turned away.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩寬厚沈毅，任重王室，曆事累世，邈為元老。

translations.literal: Changsun Song was generous, deep, and resolute, bearing the weight of the royal house, serving through many reigns, remote as a founding elder.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song was generous, deep, and resolute, bearing the weight of the royal house, serving through many reigns, remote as a founding elder.

sentences.zh: 生則宗臣，歿祀清廟，美矣！

translations.literal: Alive he was a pillar minister; dead he is sacrificed in the clear temple—beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: In life a pillar of the state; in death honored in the clear temple—how fine!

sentences.zh: 儉器識明允，智謀通贍，堂堂焉有公輔之望，謇謇焉有王臣之節。

translations.literal: Jian's capacity and insight were bright and fair, his stratagems penetrating and ample; towering, he had the look of a chief minister; stern and upright, he had a king's minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's capacity and insight were bright and fair, his stratagems penetrating and ample; towering, he had the look of a chief minister; stern and upright, he had a king's minister's integrity.

sentences.zh: 而處朝廷之日少，在方嶽之日多，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet his days in the court were few and his days on the frontier many—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet why were his days at court so few and his days on the frontier so many?

sentences.zh: 平識具該通，出內流譽，取諸開物成務，蓋亦有隋之榱桷也。

translations.literal: Ping's knowledge was comprehensive and penetrating; within and without his fame flowed; taken from opening things and completing tasks, he was perhaps also a rafter beam for Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's knowledge was comprehensive and penetrating; within and without his fame flowed; taken from opening things and completing tasks, he was perhaps also a rafter beam for Sui.

sentences.zh: 道生恭慎廉約，兼著威名，見知明主，聲入歌奏。

translations.literal: Daosheng was respectful, cautious, frugal, and restrained, and together bore a martial name; known to a bright lord, his voice entered song and performance.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was respectful, cautious, frugal, and restrained, and together bore a martial name; known to a bright lord, his voice entered song and performance.

sentences.zh: 二公並列，暉炫朝野，門祉世祿，榮被後昆。

translations.literal: The two dukes stood side by side, their brilliance dazzling court and countryside; their house's blessing and hereditary salary, glory covering later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The two dukes stood side by side, their brilliance dazzling court and countryside; their house's blessing and hereditary salary, glory covering later generations.

sentences.zh: 雖漢世八王，無以方其茂績；

translations.literal: Though the eight kings of Han cannot match their lush achievements;
translations.idiomatic: Though the eight kings of Han cannot match their lush achievements;

sentences.zh: 張氏七葉，不能譬此重光。

translations.literal: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot compare with this doubled glory.
translations.idiomatic: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot compare with this doubled glory.

sentences.zh: 子彥勇烈絕倫，紹遠樂聲特妙；

translations.literal: Ziyan's courage and fierceness were unmatched; Shaoyuan's music was uniquely subtle;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan's courage and fierceness were unmatched; Shaoyuan's music was uniquely subtle;

sentences.zh: 熾乃早稱英俊，覽乃獨擅雄辯。

translations.literal: Chi was early hailed as outstanding; Lan alone excelled in bold eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was early hailed as outstanding; Lan alone excelled in bold eloquence.

sentences.zh: 不然則何以並統師旅，俱司禮閣，鐘鼎不墜，且公且侯？

translations.literal: Otherwise how could they together command armies, jointly oversee the ritual offices, bells and tripods not fallen—and be both duke and marquis?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could they together command armies, jointly oversee the ritual offices, bells and tripods not fallen—and be both duke and marquis?

sentences.zh: 晟體資英武，兼包奇略。

translations.literal: Sheng's person combined heroic martial bearing and embraced singular stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's person combined heroic martial bearing and embraced singular stratagems.

sentences.zh: 因機制變，懷彼戎夷，傾巢盡落，屈膝稽顙。

translations.literal: Seizing the moment he made changes, cherishing those frontier tribes—their nests overturned and all fell, knees bent and foreheads touched the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the moment and adapted; he turned on those frontier tribes—their nests overturned and all fell, knees bent and foreheads to the ground.

sentences.zh: 塞垣絕鳴鏑之旅，渭橋有單于之拜。

translations.literal: On the border ramparts the clanging arrow-travel ceased; at the Wei Bridge there was the single chieftain's bow.
translations.idiomatic: On the border ramparts the whistling arrows fell silent; at the Wei Bridge a chieftain bowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 惠流邊朔，功光王府，保茲世祿，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: His grace flowed to the northern frontier; his merit lit the royal house— to preserve this hereditary salary, was it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: His grace flowed to the northern frontier; his merit lit the royal house— to preserve this hereditary salary, was it not fitting!

sentences.zh: 肥結髮內侍，雄武自立，軍鋒所指，罔不棄散，關、張萬人敵，未足多也。

translations.literal: Fei bound his hair and served within the palace; by martial prowess he stood on his own; wherever his army's edge pointed, none failed to scatter and flee—Guan and Zhang at ten thousand men apiece are not worth counting many.
translations.idiomatic: Fei bound his hair and served in the inner palace; by martial prowess he stood alone; wherever his army's edge pointed, foes scattered—Guan and Zhang, each a match for ten thousand, are hardly worth extra praise.

sentences.zh: 翰有父風，不殞先構，臨喪加禮，抑有由哉！

translations.literal: Han had his father's manner and did not ruin the ancestral structure; extra rites at the mourning—there was reason for it!
translations.idiomatic: Han had his father's manner and did not ruin the ancestral house; the emperor's added rites at his mourning—there was cause for that.
